title: The Church Needs to Know Its History
summary: Readers of this first volume of ‘Church History for Everyone’ won’t get a complete understanding of church history, but DeYoung provides a doorway through which ordinary Christians can learn to explore primary sources and more comprehensive surveys on their own.
summary_zh: 阅读《人人适用的教会史》第一卷的读者不会对教会史有全面的了解，但德永为普通基督徒提供了一条途径，让他们学会自行探索原始资料和更全面的综述。
title_zh: 教会需要了解自己的历史
content: Deep in the archives of my Facebook messages sits a note from a widow named Kathy. She thanked me for using church history in our weekly Bible studies. She loved learning about the early-church martyrs and the pilgrims. As a newly minted senior pastor pursuing a PhD in church history, this was the reassurance I needed. Our message thread ended with Kathy describing her chemo treatments. Like Faithful in John Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (a story new to her that strengthened her fight with cancer), Kathy endured her trials and entered the Celestial City. I usually have to defend the benefits of history to other pastors and friends of mine—but rarely with church members. I mostly encounter excitement when I direct Christians to our family history. In Church History for Everyone: The Story of Christianity from the Fall of Jerusalem to the Dawn of the Reformation , Kevin DeYoung, pastor of Christ Covenant Church and associate professor of systematic theology at Reformed Theological Seminary (Charlotte), blends rich doctrine with a pastoral tone. It’s the first of two planned volumes. DeYoung writes, “I intend this book to be a popular history rather than professional history, which means I am writing to be understood by ordinary people who are eager to learn but are not experts” (3). He’s successful in that effort. I wish Kathy could have read this book; it’s a church history for the church. History for the Church How is church history for the church actually for the church ? Well, words on a page are costly. Just like a pastor needs to cut more of his preparation and study out of his sermons than he’d like, a church history book for everyday Christians needs to value the reader’s attention. This means accepting that not every believer has the bandwidth to process all the names and details from church history we might want him or her to. There’s so much to digest, and the practical value of these names, dates, and specialized terms often don’t stick in the minds of casual readers. It’s easy for the stay-at-home mom or busy mechanic to delve into a church history book and quickly lose steam. On the other hand, oversimplifying in an attempt to make a book more accessible can move an argument from truth and falsehood. The story of our past needs the proper names, dates, and details to lead readers to experience the fruit of good historical learning. DeYoung attempts a near-impossible task: to write an introduction to church history that’s true (factually sound), good (encourages the church), and beautiful (enjoyable to read). He checks those boxes. Biographical Emphasis The most compelling histories are told through people, not periods. That explains why, “instead of a chronological encyclopedia version of history,” DeYoung takes “a biographical approach” (6). We get stories about figures like Irenaeus, Perpetua and Felicity, Athanasius, and Jan Hus. We read of Hus, As a pastor, Hus was passionate and sometimes hotheaded. His sermons also displayed a witty sense of humor. . . . Compared to most men of his age, he was not poor, but neither did he amass any fortune or have family estates to retire to. Even later when his enemies charged him with many faults and crimes, they never charged him with the typical list of priestly sins: drunkenness, sexual immorality, laziness, or opulence. (351) This approach has downsides, of course. A lot of important information gets left out. However, DeYoung recognizes that “when the author tells a story, there is a better chance that the reader might keep reading” (8). The most compelling histories are told through people. The biographical approach reinforces the fact that history often isn’t just about information transfer. “The goal in telling church history has been—for most of church history—a deliberate attempt at inspiration,” DeYoung observes. 我的Facebook留言的档案里 藏着一个叫凯西的寡妇的遗言 她感谢我在我们的每周圣经研究中使用了教会历史. 她喜欢了解早期教会的烈士和朝圣者. 作为一位在教会历史中攻读博士学位的资深牧师,这是我需要的保证。 我们的信息线结束 凯西描述她的化疗。

就像忠实于约翰·邦扬的朝圣者进步(她的新故事加强了她与癌症的战斗)一样,凯西忍受了她的考验并进入了天城。 我通常不得不为其他牧师和朋友捍卫历史利益, 当我把基督徒引向家族历史时,我大多会遇到兴奋。

在《人人教会历史:从耶路撒冷沦陷到改革黎明的基督教故事》中,Kevin DeYoung,基督盟约教会牧师和改革神学院(夏洛特)系统神学副教授,将丰富的学说与牧歌融合在一起。 这是两卷计划书中的第一卷。

DeYoung写道:“我打算这本书是一部受欢迎的历史,而不是专业历史,这意味着我写作是为了让渴望学习但并非专家的普通人理解。” (3)。 他的努力是成功的。 我希望凯西能读到这本书, 教会的历史是怎样的 教会的历史实际上为教会?

嗯,一页上的字是昂贵的。 就像牧师需要从布道中切除更多准备和学习, 这意味着接受并非每个信徒都有带宽来处理我们可能希望他或她处理的教会历史中的所有名字和细节.

这些名称、日期和专门术语的实际价值往往不会停留在临时读者的脑海里。 家庭妈妈或繁忙的技工很容易深入研究教会历史, 另一方面,为了使一本书更容易获得而过分简化,可以使一个论点从真理和谎言中转移出来。

我们过去的故事需要适当的名字,日期,细节,以引导读者体验良好的历史学习成果. DeYoung试图完成一个近乎不可能的任务:写一个教会历史的介绍,这个介绍是真实的(实际上声音),好的(鼓励教会),和美丽的(阅读的乐趣). 他检查那些箱子。

传记重点 最有说服力的历史是通过人们而不是通过时间讲述的。 这解释了为什么“而不是历史的按时间顺序的百科全书版本”,DeYoung采取“一种传记方式”(6)。 我们得到有关伊雷纳厄斯、佩佩图亚和费利西蒂、阿塔纳修斯和扬·胡斯等人物的故事。 我们读到胡斯,作为一个牧师,胡斯是热情的,有时是热头.

他的布道也表现出幽默的幽默感.  . 与他这个年龄的大多数男人相比,他并不贫穷,但他也没有积累任何财富,也没有家庭庄园可以退休. 甚至在后来他的敌人指控他有许多过失和罪行时,他们从未指控他典型的祭司罪列表:醉酒,性不道德,懒惰,或奢侈.

(351) 当然,这种做法有缺点。 很多重要信息被忽略. 然而,DeYoung承认,“当作者讲述一个故事时,读者继续阅读的可能性更大。” (8)。 最有说服力的历史是通过人们讲述的。 历史往往不只是信息传递。

title: Leverage Church History for Ministry
summary: Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan discuss how pastors can use church history to strengthen their preaching, encourage their congregations, understand historic Christian beliefs, and learn from believers who have gone before us.
summary_zh: 马特·斯梅瑟斯特（Matt Smethurst）和利根·邓肯（Ligon Duncan）讨论了牧师如何利用教会历史来强化讲道、激励会众、理解历史上的基督教信仰，并向先辈信徒学习。
title_zh: 利用教会历史开展事工
content: Why should pastors care about church history, and how can they use it in everyday ministry? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan discuss why church history is more than a subject for scholars. They share practical ways pastors can draw from Christian biographies, historical events, and the early church to strengthen their preaching and help their congregations grow in faith. title: How to Preach to Workers
summary: The New Testament offers two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching.
summary_zh: 新约提供了两种范式，说明传道人如何在教导中考虑到工人。
title_zh: 如何向工人传福音
content: I still remember the first time I heard a sermon on God’s design for work. Pastor Colin Smith was in a series working through the Ten Commandments, and he’d come to the fourth command about the Sabbath. I was expecting to hear challenging words about rest. So I was surprised when he spent the first half of his sermon talking about work. Because he’s a good exegetical preacher, Smith reminded us to pay attention to the part of the passage we might overlook: “Six days you shall labor, and do all your work . . .” (Ex. 20:9). For 16 minutes, Smith preached about God’s design for work. He explained how God modeled work in creation, crafting and making our world like a builder, engineer, and artist. And since humans were created in the likeness of this God, our labors are a significant part of what it means to represent him in the world. Then he started naming regular kinds of work—such as the school crossing guard who creates a zone of safety and protection for children. He shared example after example, even naming those who are were unemployed and looking for work as engaging in a form of dignified labor. They can please God as they trust him to provide and remain diligent to seek out what’s next. At the time, I was working a summer landscaping job between semesters at seminary. I took the job because it was necessary, not because I found it personally fulfilling or spiritually significant. I’d been subconsciously wanting to be done with mowing lawns and picking weeds so I could get back to the important work of studying Scripture. But God used Smith’s sermon to reorient my ordinary labor. Preaching with workers in mind is vital to shepherding a congregation. It reminds church members that work is a primary context for discipleship and helps them work out the implications of God’s Word where they spend a large portion of their time. The New Testament gives two paradigms for how preachers can consider workers in their teaching. Work as an Illustration of the Kingdom As the eternal, perfect Son of God, Jesus isn’t only Savior and Lord but also the most brilliant teacher the world has ever heard. Therefore, as preachers, we take his pedagogy seriously even as we learn his precepts and mimic his practices. Jesus often proclaims the good news by igniting people’s imaginations and explaining eternal truths in concrete realities, including the body (Matt. 6:22; 7:3–5; 24:7–8), nature (Matt. 6:28–29; Mark 11:23; Luke 17:6), and food (Matt. 13:33; John 6:35, 53–56). But Jesus’s most consistent metaphor for the truths of the kingdom is work and workers. Klaus Issler’s survey reveals that of the 37 parables in the Synoptic Gospels, 32 reference work or workers, representing 22 different work roles. In 25 of the parables, work is a main part of the storyline. Here are examples: The farmer sows the seed (Matt. 13). The faithful manager gives the servants of the household food at the proper time (Luke 12:42). Even an unjust judge will give a persistent widow justice (18:1–8). The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (John 10:11). A king going into battle should take counsel to see if he’s strong enough before he a ttacks (Luke 14:31). When Jesus describes what it meant to follow him and live in his kingdom, why does he use the ordinary language of work and workers? First, God’s self-disclosure is often wrapped in the language of work. For instance, he’s portrayed as a composer and performer (Deut. 31:19), a tentmaker (Job 9:8), a garment maker and dresser (29:14), a shepherd (Ps. 23:1–4), a builder (Prov. 8:27–31), a metalworker (Isa. 1:24–26), a potter (31:9), and a farmer (Hos. 10:11). If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. If God is the original worker, it makes sense that the whole realm of work can teach us his ways. 由于他是一个优秀的传教士,史密斯提醒我们注意我们可能忽略的那段话:"六天你必须努力,并做你所有的工作."(前20:9). 16分钟,史密斯宣扬上帝的工作设计. 他解释了上帝如何塑造我们的世界 像一个建筑师、工程师和艺术家

由于人类是在这个上帝的相似之处创造的, 我们的劳动是世界中代表他的意义的重要部分. 然后,他开始点名从事常规工作,例如学校越野警卫,为儿童创造一个安全和保护的地区。

他举了个例子,甚至将那些失业和寻找工作的人命名为从事一种有尊严的劳动。 他们可以取悦上帝, 因为他们相信上帝提供, 当时我在神学院的暑期园林设计工作

它提醒教会成员,工作是门徒活动的主要背景,帮助他们解决神话的影响,在那里他们花费了大量的时间. "新约"为传教士如何在教学中考虑工人给出了两种范式.

发挥王国的作用 耶稣不仅是救世主, 因此,作为传教士,我们在学习他的戒律和模仿他的做法时,也认真对待他的教学方法.

耶稣经常通过点燃人们的想象力和在具体现实中解释永恒的真理来宣告好消息,包括身体(Matt 6:22;7:3–5;24:7–8),自然(Matt 6:28–29;Mark 11:23;Luke 17:6)和食物(Matt 13:33;John 6:35,53–56). 但耶稣对王国真理最一致的比喻是工作和工人.

Klaus Issler的调查表明,在Synoptic福音书中的37个比喻中,有32个参考工作或工人,代表着22个不同的工作角色. 在25个比喻中,作品是故事情节的主要部分. 以下是例子:农民播种(Matt.13). 忠诚的经理在适当的时候给家庭食物的仆人(公爵12:42).

首先,上帝的自我披露常常用工作语言包扎。 例如,他被描绘成作曲家和表演者(德国31:19)、帐篷匠(约旦9:8)、制衣和梳妆师(29:14)、牧羊人(Ps.23:1-4)、建筑师(Prov.8:27-31)、金属工人(Isa:1:24-26)、锅工(31:9)和农民(Hos:10:11)。

title: In the Darkness, Christmas Shines a Light
summary: The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves.
summary_zh: 神所创造的秩序——黑暗与光明、黑夜与白昼——的普遍启示，使每一受造物都认识到自己需要光明，需要来自自身之外的拯救。
title_zh: 在黑暗中，圣诞节照亮光明
content: Read For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and thick darkness the peoples; but the LORD will arise upon you, and his glory will be seen upon you. And nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising. (Isa. 60:2–3) Reflect There’s something about a sunrise. It wakes the world. Unlike the jarring blare of an alarm clock, a sunrise quietly whispers “Wake, O sleeper” with the graceful love of a parent rubbing a sleeping child’s back. When the sun rises, the slumbering stir to life. We’ve just spent seven or eight hours dead to the world. Then the sunrise triggers in us what looks like a resurrection. We rise. Certain flowers—daisies, poppies, and the aptly named morning glories—open their blossoms at the sun’s rising. Little by little, empty streets fill and quiet houses stir. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. Drawn to the warmth and energy of the just-unveiled sun, we transition from rest to work, stillness to activity. It’s not surprising that the sun is an oft-used metaphor for God. For he, too, resurrects the dead. He, too, is the Giver of life and growth. He, too, draws all things to himself—such as the trees, which by nature grow upward, toward the sun, their branches like arms raised in perpetual worship. This is the created order. All things were made to be drawn to and sustained by the sun. We were made to be alive insofar as we live, grow, and flourish by solar energy. So too with God. We’re in darkness and death without him. As he bestows his grace on us, we rise to new life. We’re able to grow. Like the sunflower blossom, which turns to follow the sun wherever it’s positioned in the sky, we’re created to look to the Lord, who “will arise upon [us], and his glory will be seen upon [us]” (Isa. 60:2). In a world of darkness, we ache for the light. We wait for the sunrise. All nations, all kings, all people share this in common. The horizon each of us looks to—the nature of the “new day” we await—may be different: A new job. A remodeled home. A regime change. But only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. His is “the true light, which gives light to everyone” (John 1:9). Isaiah’s prophecy was fulfilled in him. Only the sunrise of Christ will eternally satisfy. The general revelation of God’s created order—darkness and light, night and day—primes every created thing to know they need light, a salvation from outside themselves. The special revelation of Christ reveals a truer light than even the sun: the light that is our eternal life, the light the darkness will never overcome (v. 5), the light that will one day end night as we know it (Rev. 22:5). Respond How is God’s glory seen in your life? How are you reflecting his beauty? In contrast to those who dwell in darkness, how does your life reflect 1 Thessalonians 5:5: “You are all children of light, children of the day. We are not of the night or of the darkness”?

我们每个人期待的地平线——我们等待的 " 新日 " 的性质——可能不同:新的工作。 一座重修的故乡. 政权更迭. 但只有基督的日出才能永远满足. 他的作品是“真正的光,它为每个人带来光明”(约翰1:9)。 以赛亚的预言在他身上得到了实现. 只有基督的日出才能永远满足

真主所创造的秩序——黑暗和光明,昼夜——的启示,使每一个被创造的事物都明白,他们需要光明,这是外部的拯救。 基督的特别启示揭示出比太阳更真实的光芒:即我们永恒生命的光芒,黑暗永远不会战胜的光芒(v. 5),即我们所知道的一天末夜的光芒(Rev.22: 5).

title: How to Fire Someone at a Christian Organization
summary: If managers do their jobs well, believe that God is sovereign, and bring the love of Christ even into hard conversations, everyone will be better off.
summary_zh: 如果管理者能做好自己的工作，相信神掌管一切，即使在艰难的谈话中也能流露出基督的爱，那么每个人都会受益。
title_zh: 如何在基督教组织中解雇某人
content: Over the course of my career, I’ve participated in more than 190 exits of employees, whether I was coaching a manager, planning upstream, sitting in on calls, or orchestrating layoffs. Each time was tough. Parting ways with an employee is one of the heaviest things a manager does. Doing it both clearly and kindly takes a lot of preparation and emotional regulation. In a faith-based workplace, these decisions can be even more surprising and hurtful, because managers try to spare the discomfort of a conversation about performance under any number of banners of being “kind.” How should we think about this as Christians who manage other Christians? Why Good Work Is Important A church’s mission is to spread the good news of Jesus, create ways for people to know him more deeply, and love our neighbors. A Christian nonprofit’s purpose is adjacent—to provide mercy, justice, evangelism, or discipleship while pointing people to Christ and their local church. This work happens through ministry and outreach staff, but also through effective operations. Doing this work takes all types of roles: pastors, administrators, and ministry coordinators; managers, accountants, and musicians; executive admins, facilities operators, and IT teams. Much of what it takes to run a church or Christian organization happens outside the hours of direct ministry. To do any of this well, churches and nonprofits must hire capable people who can effectively perform their duties and steward the mission. When managers in a secular workplace don’t hire wisely, I’ve seen the result in poor functional performance, departmental infighting, disengagement, acrimonious exits, and abuse of company resources. In a faith-based organization or church, you may get a mix of this and something worse: the spread of the gospel can be compromised too. Upstream Work for Managers As a manager, if you notice someone isn’t performing well, the best time to start talking about it isn’t at the exit conversation. It’s way upstream from that. Your core job is to ensure your people have what they need to be successful. That includes clear expectations, communication of what success looks like, feedback on performance, and accountability for meeting those standards. Ideally, you’re doing these on a regular basis in one-on-one meetings  and in performance check-ins throughout the year. Churches and nonprofits must hire capable people who can effectively perform their duties and steward the mission. This is a manager’s job, and faith-based organizations don’t have a softer standard. Where I’ve seen termination decisions and conversations go south—in Christian organizations or elsewhere—is when a manager doesn’t understand this. (Or, worse, they understand it but think that somehow it doesn’t apply to them.) Speaking to an employee about parting ways because you’ve consistently documented underperformance is a rough conversation. It’s far worse when your failure to give regular feedback leaves an employee blindsided, confused, and hurt when you need to broach termination. Often, that failure is rooted in a desire to avoid conflict or hurt feelings. The manager would rather spare himself the discomfort of a direct conversation. In a Christian organization, this impulse pulls hard. The employees under your care all love Jesus. They’re there to promote the church’s mission and spread the gospel. You may even sit shoulder to shoulder in the pews with them on Sundays. But James 4:17 has a word for managers who fail to do the difficult work: “Whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.” Colossians 4:1 underlines this: “Masters, treat your bondservants justly and fairly, knowing that you also have a Master in heaven.” I’ve watched managers avoid the perceived sin of commission (telling someone he’s doing a poor job in his role) and step right into the sin of omission (letting the problem fester until the employee is struggling and a termination conversation seems inevit

title_zh: 南苏丹戈罗姆难民营的礼拜者遭遇暴力袭击
content: Around 8:30 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 15, the courtyard of the Darfur Christian Council church in Gorom Refugee Camp near Juba, South Sudan, became a scene of sudden violence. As worshippers gathered for prayer, a group led by Baqir Muhammad Saleh launched a brutal attack. Stones were thrown, sticks were used to beat people, and some victims were bitten and strangled. “Pastor Daniel Hassan suffered severe injuries: a large part of his left ear was lost to a bite, and the tendon in his middle finger was damaged,” a local bishop who wished to remain anonymous said. “Pastor Samuel Omer received serious blows to the head that caused internal injuries. His wife was beaten in the abdominal area and sustained internal trauma. Brother Michael Yusuf was struck in the nose, while Brother Elias Ibrahim Mohammed was strangled and beaten on the stomach, resulting in minor injuries. Others, including Ahmed Khalid and Fatima Ahmed Khalid, were also exposed to the violence.” This was not the first time the church courtyard had been attacked. On April 17, 2025, Pastor Hassan was shot, sustaining injuries to his thigh and hand. The repeated nature of these assaults has left the congregation shaken and deeply concerned for their safety. “We continue to pray for peace and forgiveness, asking believers to restrain themselves and offer words of love, because the church is a place of holiness and prayer. As the Psalmist writes, ‘Turn from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it’ (Psalm 34:14). Christ teaches us to forgive and to be a blessing even in the face of hatred.” Hassan stated. The Darfur Christian Council serves believers who have already fled conflict and persecution in Sudan. For many, the refugee camp was meant to be a place of relative safety. Instead, the church has become a target. The latest attack has deepened fear among worshippers, many of whom now wonder whether they can gather freely to pray without risking further violence. “We demand that the authorities in the camp provide as much protection as possible to the worshippers,” another victim said. “We also demand that a proper investigation be carried out and that justice be done according to the law. The Lord is a God of justice; ‘He will judge the world in righteousness and the peoples with equity’ (Psalm 98:9). We cry out for that justice to be seen here.” Despite the pain and injury, the leaders of the Darfur Christian Council have chosen the path of restraint and faith. They continue to call their people to respond with the love of Christ rather than retaliation, holding fast to the truth that the church must remain a place of peace and holiness even when surrounded by hostility. “Though the attack has wounded our bodies and our hearts, we refuse to abandon the way of the cross,” Pastor Hassan said. “‘The Lord is close to the broken-hearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit’ (Psalm 34:18). We trust him to heal our wounds, protect his people, and turn this suffering into a testimony of his grace.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post Violence Strikes Worshippers in South Sudan’s Gorom Refugee Camp first appeared on International Christian Concern .
content_zh:
11月15日星期日上午8时30分左右,位于南苏丹朱巴附近Gorom难民营的达尔富尔基督教会教堂的庭院成为突然发生暴力事件的场所. 当礼拜者聚集祈祷时,由Baqir Muhammad Saleh率领的一个团体发动了残酷的攻击。 投掷石块,用棍棒打人,一些受害者被咬死并勒死.

当地一位希望匿名的主教说,“Daniel Hassan牧师受重伤:左耳大部被咬伤,中指的阴茎受损”。 “Samuel Omer神父头部受到严重打击,造成内伤。 他的妻子在腹部遭到殴打,并受到内伤。

Michael Yusuf兄弟被击中鼻子,而Elias Ibrahim Mohammed兄弟被勒死并殴打腹部,造成轻伤。 其他人,包括艾哈迈德·哈立德和法蒂玛·艾哈迈德·哈立德也遭到暴力。 这不是教堂庭院第一次遭到袭击。 2025年4月17日,哈桑牧师中弹,大腿和手受伤.

这些袭击一再发生,使教会感到动摇,并深为关切其安全。 “我们继续祈求和平和宽恕,要求信徒克制,献出爱语,因为教堂是神圣和祈祷的地方。 如"诗经"所记载:"从恶反善;求和而追之(诗经34:14).

基督教导我们,即使面对仇恨,也要宽恕和成为祝福。” 哈桑说。 达尔富尔基督教理事会为已经逃离苏丹冲突和迫害的信徒服务。 对许多人来说,难民营是相对安全的地方。 相反,教堂已经成为目标.

最近的一次袭击加深了礼拜者的恐惧,其中许多人现在怀疑他们是否可以自由聚集在一起祈祷,而不会面临进一步暴力的风险。 另一位受害者说,“我们要求难民营当局向礼拜者提供尽可能多的保护。” “我们还要求进行适当调查,并依法伸张正义。

主是正义的神; " 他将以正义和公平来评判世界和人民 " (第98:9段)。 我们要求在这里看到这种正义。” 尽管遭受了痛苦和伤害,但达尔富尔基督教理事会的领导人选择了克制和信仰的道路。

他们继续号召自己的人民以基督的爱而不是报复来回应,坚守真理,即即使周围充满敌意,教会也必须保持和平和神圣。 “尽管袭击伤害了我们的身体和心灵,但我们拒绝放弃十字架的道路,”哈桑牧师说。

" `主近于伤心者,救精神所压者'(34:18). 我们信任他医治我们的创伤,保护他的人民,并把这种痛苦变成他恩惠的见证。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

title_zh: 尼日利亚19岁基督徒农民在袭击中失去一只手
content: A 19-year-old Christian farmer, Jesse Monday, lost one of his hands after suspected Fulani herdsmen attacked three young men working on their farmland in Rewienku Village, Miango District, Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau state, on Monday, Nov. 23. The attack reportedly occurred around 3 p.m. when the three young men were working on their farm. Monday sustained multiple machete wounds, and his hand was completely severed during the assault. He is currently receiving medical treatment at an undisclosed hospital. The other two young men escaped without physical injuries, according to a statement issued by the Rewienku Youth Development Association (RYDA). Rewienku is a predominantly farming community in Miango District, part of the Irigwe-speaking area of Bassa LGA in Plateau state’s central region. Residents depend largely on agriculture for their livelihoods. In a statement signed by its general secretary, Comr. Vokwe Joshua Obadiah, RYDA called on the Plateau State Government, Bassa Local Government Council and security agencies to investigate the attack, identify those responsible and prosecute the perpetrators. The association also demanded increased security deployments in Rewienku and surrounding farmlands to protect residents from further attacks. It appealed to the government and humanitarian organizations to provide medical assistance and rehabilitation support for Monday. RYDA urged community leaders, the Rigwe Development Association and the Irigwe Youth Movement to work with security agencies to address threats to residents. The association also appealed to residents, particularly young people, to remain calm, avoid retaliation, and report credible information to security authorities. A Growing Problem According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. The network of militias is responsible for four times more civilian deaths than the two prominent Islamic terror organizations, Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), combined. The study’s findings challenge the commonly held belief that the two organized terror groups kill the larger number of Christians, highlighting the Fulani network’s expanded efforts to target Christians. title_zh: 印度一个有8口人的基督徒家庭被驱逐，无家可归
content: A Christian family of eight in the Sukma district of Chhattisgarh, India, was left homeless after Hindu nationalists ransacked and demolished their home on the morning of Nov. 16. During the eviction, the family’s essential household items — including food, clothing, bedding, kitchen utensils, and vital personal documents — were thrown out of their home. The house, belonging to Manglu Sodi and his wife, Hirmibai, was reportedly ransacked and demolished because of their Christian faith. Amid the destruction, 4,000 rupees (roughly $43), about five grams of gold, and a bicycle were stolen before the house was destroyed. Relief in Safe House Fleeing for their safety, the family traveled roughly 40 miles to reach the district headquarters of Sukma, where they were placed in a Safe House constructed with the help of International Christian Concern (ICC). Representatives of the Progressive Christian Alliance (PCA), a rights advocacy group working for the welfare of Christian minorities, coordinated with local pastor Harendra Madiya in Sukma to provide relief for the persecuted family. PCA State Coordinator Patras Balti visited the family to encourage and pray with them, urging them to remain steadfast in their faith despite the severe hardship. Although formal complaints have been submitted to the local police station, the Superintendent of Police (SP), and the district collector of Sukma, no formal inquiry or legal action has been initiated to date. Without their identification documents or savings, the family faces steep hurdles in rehabilitation and rebuilding their lives. Historic Church Building Razed Down In another development, up north of Sukma district, about 300 miles away, a historic church estimated by locals to be roughly 130 years old was demolished in Rajnandgaon district of Chhattisgarh in the past week. The structure was part of the campus of the Missionary Bands of the World Leprosy Hospital (also known as the Rajnandgaon Leprosy Hospital and Clinics), which stood on about 23 acres of government-leased land originally allotted for treating and rehabilitating leprosy patients. The Clearance Operation The demolition followed a lease-cancellation order issued on Nov. 6 by the Rajnandgaon district collector. The demolition drive razed not only the church, but also the old hospital wards, administrative offices, and residential quarters of the leprosy hospital. The administration said the reclaimed land will be used for public amenities, including a sports ground. However, Christian watchdogs are skeptical about the district collector’s action. Christian community leaders urged a clear distinction between the government’s right to recover land over alleged lease violations and the decision to destroy a heritage religious structure. 这所房子属于Manglu Sodi和他的妻子Hirmibai,据说因其基督教信仰而被洗劫和拆毁。 在破坏中,4000卢比(约43美元),约5克黄金,还有一辆自行车在房屋被摧毁之前被盗.

在安全屋救济他们的安全,他们一家大约走40英里到达Sukma区总部,在那里他们被安置在国际基督教关注组织的帮助下建造的安全屋里。

进步基督教联盟(PCA)的代表,这是一个致力于基督教少数派福利的权利倡导团体,与苏克马的Harendra Madiya当地牧师协调,为受迫害的家庭提供救济. 常设仲裁法院州协调员Patras Balti访问了该家庭,鼓励他们和他们一起祈祷,敦促他们尽管面临严重困难,但仍要坚定信仰。

尽管已经向地方警察局、警察局长和Sukma地区收藏家提出了正式申诉,但迄今尚未启动任何正式的调查或法律行动。 没有身份证或储蓄,家庭在恢复和重建生活方面面临巨大障碍。

历史教堂建筑 在另一项发展中,在大约300英里外的Sukma区北部,当地人估计大约130年历史的一座历史教堂在上周在恰蒂斯加尔邦的Rajnandgaon区被拆除。

该建筑是世界麻风病医院(又称拉杰南德加翁麻风病医院和诊所)传教团校园的一部分,占地约23英亩,最初分配用于治疗和康复麻风病人。 清除行动 拆除是在11月签发的租约取消令之后进行的。

6 由拉杰南德加翁区收藏家. 拆除运动不仅夷平了教堂,还夷平了麻风医院的旧医院病房,行政办公室和住宅区. 行政当局说,开垦的土地将用于公共设施,包括体育场。 但基督教监督员对地区收藏家的行为持怀疑态度。

summary_zh: 这可能令人感到意外，但圣诞节是伊拉克的国定假日——自2018年12月政府正式宣布以来一直如此。“这感觉像是为了显得不歧视而采取的象征性举措。”“彼得罗斯”说道。他是一名亚述基督徒，与一个伊拉克侨民家庭一起居住在美国。他补充说，这种“象征性”的庆祝……   这篇题为《圣诞节在伊拉克是一个喜忧参半的节日》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
title_zh: 圣诞节是伊拉克一个喜忧参半的节日
content: This may come as a surprise, but Christmas is a national holiday in Iraq — ever since the government formally declared it so in December 2018. “It feels like a token move to appear non-discriminatory,” said “Petros,” an Assyrian Christian living in the U.S. with an Iraqi expat family. He added that this “token” celebration of Christmas “ignores the native traditions” of the region’s Christians and “instead opts for a European-style Christmas” with Santa Claus and various types of Christmas trees that don’t naturally grow in the area. Iraq, which was already celebrating the birth of Christ when most of Europe was still pagan, has among the world’s oldest Christian communities, with the faith arriving in the first century A.D. Petros feels that the Iraqi government’s acknowledgment of Christmas is more of a public relations strategy to deflect from the recent horrors faced by Iraq’s Christians. “Yonita,” an Assyrian woman who is Chaldean Catholic and lives in the U.S., believes the recent recognition of Christmas is financially motivated. “Iraq is trying to rebuild itself,” she said, adding that it might be “taking notes” from more successful countries in the region that have comparatively more religious freedom. Yonita suspects that celebrating Christmas could be an attempt at showing camaraderie with the West. It could also be a way to make the homeland seem more congenial to the many Iraqi Christians abroad. As she pointed out, the Christian Iraqi diaspora tends to be quite well-off financially. “There was a formal call inviting us back to Iraq [to] invest in the rebuilding of the cradle of civilization,” Yonita said. A Sad Reality Whatever the Iraqi government’s true motivation, one painful aspect is hard to deny: By the time Christmas became a national holiday, most Iraqi Christians had already been driven out of their homeland. Conditions were so difficult during the previous 15 years that the country had lost up to 90% of its Christian community. Iraq’s remaining Christians, most of whom belong either to the Chaldean Catholic Church or the Assyrian Church of the East, now comprise less than half of 1% of the country’s overall population. The Christian population had already seen considerable decline during the 24-year reign of former Iraqi president Saddam Hussein, a man of immense sadism. But, for all his homicidal flaws, Hussein — though Muslim by background — was no Islamic extremist. In fact, his longtime right-hand man, Deputy Prime Minister Tariq Aziz, was a Christian, at least technically. It would likely be an exaggeration to say that Hussein cared about the welfare of Iraqi Christians, but the bone-crushing force of his reputation rendered most Iraqis, regardless of their faith, too intimidated to indulge in sectarian hostilities. Petros said that his fellow Assyrian Christians “either liked Hussein for providing stability and jobs, or hated him for killing their family members.” Many of Iraq’s Christians wanted him to stay in power only because they had an acute sense of the mayhem that would erupt after their secular tyrant was deposed. “It’s like the saying goes,” Petros said. “Better to deal with the devil you know than the devil you don’t.” At this point, though, both “devils” have fully acquainted themselves with Iraq. The Rise of Extremism The ousting of Hussein from power in 2003 brought in an era of rising Islamic extremism, most notably with the Islamic State group (ISIS), formerly known as “al-Qaida in Iraq.” Some Iraqi Christians were even accused of collaborating with the U.S. military. As the atmosphere grew increasingly precarious in post-Hussein Iraq, most Christians fled the country, having decided the other options — violent death, forced conversion, or paying a religious tax — were unpalatable. Those who remained were often hunted. In June 2007, in the northern Iraqi city of Mosul, a priest and his assistants were killed right in front of his church. 这也许是个惊喜, 但圣诞节是伊拉克的国庆节, “Petros”是一位居住在美国的亚述基督教徒,

他补充说,这种对该地区基督教徒的圣诞节 " 玷污当地传统 " 的 " 庆祝 " , " 而不是选择一个欧洲式的圣诞节 " ,圣诞老人和该地区自然不会生长的各类圣诞树。

伊拉克在庆祝基督诞生时,欧洲大部分地区仍然是异教徒,伊拉克是世界上最古老的基督教社区之一,公元一世纪时,信仰就已经降临。 彼得罗斯认为伊拉克政府承认圣诞节更是一种公共关系策略,旨在转移伊拉克基督徒最近面临的恐怖。

“Yonita”是一位信奉迦勒底天主教、居住在美国的亚述妇女, 她说,“伊拉克正在努力重建自己”,她补充说,它可能“注意到”该区域比较成功的宗教自由的国家。

Yonita怀疑庆祝圣诞节可能是试图与西方展示友情. 这也可以成为使祖国看起来对海外许多伊拉克基督徒更加融洽的方法. 正如她指出的那样,伊拉克的基督教散居国外者往往在财政上相当富裕。

Yonita说,“有人正式邀请我们回到伊拉克,投资重建文明的摇篮。” 一个悲哀的现实 无论伊拉克政府的真正动机如何,一个痛苦的方面很难否认: 到圣诞节成为国家节日时,大多数伊拉克基督徒已经被驱逐出家园.

在过去15年里,情况十分困难,以至于该国丧失了90%的基督教徒。 伊拉克其余的基督教徒,大多属于迦勒底天主教会或东方亚述教会,现在占该国总人口的不到1%。

伊拉克前总统萨达姆·侯赛因24年的统治期间,基督教徒人数已经大幅度减少,他是一位极度虐待的人。 但是,侯赛因尽管有穆斯林背景,但他的杀人缺陷并非伊斯兰极端主义分子。 事实上,他长期担任右手的副总理塔里克·阿齐兹是基督徒,至少在技术上是这样.

如果说侯赛因关心伊拉克基督徒的福利,那很可能是一种夸张的说法,但他的名声的骨折力量使大多数伊拉克人,无论其信仰如何,都过于恐吓,不敢陷入教派敌对行动。

Petros说,他的亚述基督徒同胞“要么喜欢侯赛因提供稳定和工作,要么恨他杀害家人”。 许多伊拉克基督徒希望他继续掌权,只是因为他们对世俗暴君被废黜后爆发的混乱有强烈的感受。 Petros说,

“最好对付你认识的恶魔, 然而,此时,这两个“恶魔”已完全熟悉伊拉克。

极端主义的兴起 2003年侯赛因被赶下台,带来了伊斯兰极端主义抬头的时代,其中最突出的是伊斯兰国集团(ISIS),它以前被称为“伊拉克基地组织”。 一些伊拉克基督徒甚至被指控与美国军方勾结.

由于后侯赛因的伊拉克气氛越来越不稳定,大多数基督徒逃离该国,决定了其他选择——暴力死亡、强迫皈依或缴纳宗教税——是令人不快的。 留下来的人经常遭到追捕。 2007年6月,在伊拉克北部城市摩苏尔,一名牧师及其助手在他教堂前被杀死。

title_zh: 为巴基斯坦基督徒的释放而进行的呼吁工作变得更加紧迫
content: Shahzad Masih has been praying for justice since 2017. He was just 16 years old when he was arrested on false charges, and has been waiting to be hanged since 2022. Nine years later, the American Center for Law and Justice (ACLJ), through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), is continuing to advocate for his release, Christian Daily International reported. In 2017, Masih was working as a janitor at a hospital when a Muslim coworker asked him about his belief in Jesus. As he explained his faith, he mentioned a comment made by a family friend that was spoken against the Prophet Muhammad, which offended the coworker and ended the conversation. The coworker belonged to Tehreek-e-Tahfuz-e-Islam, a conservative Islamic group in Pakistan. Members of the group heard about their conversation and confronted the Masih. Though he tried to clarify the situation, he was handed over to the police on July 13, 2017, and was questioned without legal representation before being imprisoned. In November 2022, according to Section 295C of the Pakistan Penal Code, he was sentenced to death for the “use of derogatory remarks, etc. in respect of the Holy Prophet.” Since then, he has been waiting to be hanged for his unjust sentence. The United Nations has called for his immediate release, stating that these decisions deny his right to “freedom of expression.” OLA has supported him and filed an appeal for his freedom four times, but the Lahore High Court has yet to hear his case. “Shahzad Masih was just 16 years old when he was arrested, and nine years later, he remains on death row for allegedly reporting someone else’s words,” said CeCe Heil, senior counsel and international legal director for the ACLJ. “We urge Pakistani authorities to uphold fundamental human rights, overturn this unjust conviction, and bring Shahzad Masih home to his family.” One of Many As more stories of Christians being imprisoned for false blasphemy accusations arise this year — including Amir Peter , who was tried before by a Lahore court in 2024 and died in custody in July — ACLJ is committed more than ever to fighting for the life of this young Christian. “This is the ultimate abominable human rights violation, and we’ll take this case all the way to Pakistan’s Supreme Court,” the advocacy group wrote . Open Doors ranks Pakistan as the eighth most dangerous place to be a Christian in the world. They are constantly subjected to persecution through discrimination, death threats, mob violence, imprisonment, and death, through its Pakistani counterpart, the Organization for Legal Aid (OLA), continues. title_zh: 越南在教会土地纠纷中拆除历史悠久的天主教建筑
content: Vietnamese authorities demolished a historic building belonging to the Redemptorist Catholic community in the central city of Huế on Tuesday, escalating a decades-long dispute over church property and raising renewed concerns about religious freedom in the communist-governed country. The demolition of the L’Accueil building followed the deployment of police by local authorities to block roads surrounding the Redemptorist monastery and Our Lady of Perpetual Help Church. Electricity to the area was also cut, preventing some parishioners from reaching the church to attend Mass or express solidarity with the religious community. According to the Redemptorists, heavy machinery began demolishing the structure while priests, religious brothers, and parishioners gathered nearby in prayer. The demolition continued through Nov. 18, leaving the property leveled and fenced off. The Redemptorist Provincial Chapter of Vietnam condemned the operation, arguing that authorities proceeded despite unresolved legal questions and repeated requests to review the property’s ownership. “Justice cannot be established through force, and the truth cannot be erased along with the structures that have been demolished,” the congregation said in a Nov. 17 statement as the demolition was proceeding. Communist Land Takeover The dispute centers on land that the Redemptorists purchased in 1930. According to historical documentation cited by the religious order, Huế municipal authorities formally recognized the congregation’s ownership in 1971. The L’Accueil complex was subsequently developed on the property between 1938 and 1943. It served as a center for educational, cultural, and community activities, housing a library, auditorium, and reading room. A sawmill was also established on the grounds in the 1950s, providing local employment. Following the communist takeover of South Vietnam in 1975, the government’s relationship with religious institutions changed significantly. Church properties throughout the country came under increasing state control, with religious communities frequently losing access to land and buildings they had previously owned. The Redemptorists maintain that they never voluntarily surrendered their rights to the L’Accueil property. They acknowledge that the congregation transferred assets associated with a sawmill to the state in 1978, but argue that the transfer did not include the land itself. Authorities subsequently assigned the property to government-controlled institutions. The remaining parcel, measuring about 2,550 square meters, is currently managed by a local sports vocational school. Recent Efforts The congregation has sought the property’s return since 1994. Its most recent formal complaint, submitted to the Huế People’s Committee on Oct. 24, requested recognition of its land-use rights and clarification of the property’s legal status. Authorities reportedly rejected the complaint in a Nov. 8 response, stating that it had no basis for consideration. A notice posted at the property in October announced plans to develop a public park and parking lot on the site. Local authorities have defended the project as serving public interests, including improving traffic conditions and providing additional green space in a densely populated area. Vietnamese law establishes that land is collectively owned by the people and administered by the state. Government authorities have also invoked a 2003 National Assembly resolution that generally prevents reconsideration of certain land and housing arrangements established before July 1, 1991. The Redemptorists, however, dispute the government’s interpretation of the property’s history and say authorities have not adequately explained the legal grounds for demolishing the building. They have asked officials to publicly disclose the documentation supporting their decision and review the historical records presented by the congregation. content_zh:
越南当局星期二在胡瓦克市中心拆除了属于救赎派天主教社团的一座历史建筑,使长达数十年的教会财产纠纷升级,再次引起共产主义统治下的国家的宗教自由问题.

在L ' Accueil大楼被拆除之前,地方当局部署了警察,封锁救赎会修道院和永生圣母助教周围的道路。 该地区的电力也被切断,使一些教区人士无法前往教堂参加弥撒或表示对宗教界的声援.

据救赎派说,重型机械开始拆除该建筑,而祭司,宗教兄弟,以及教区教徒聚集在附近祈祷. 拆除工作一直持续到11月18日,财产被夷为平地和围起来。

越南救赎主义省分会谴责了这次行动,认为当局不顾尚未解决的法律问题和一再要求审查该财产的所有权而继续行动. “正义不能通过武力建立,真理不能与被拆除的建筑物一起抹去。”

17份在拆除过程中的声明。 共产党夺地 争端集中在救赎者在1930年购买的土地上。 根据宗教秩序所引用的历史文献,胡瓦克市当局于1971年正式承认该教会的所有权. L ' Accueil建筑群后来于1938年至1943年间在地产上发展.

它作为教育、文化和社区活动中心、图书馆、礼堂和阅览室。 1950年代还在当地建立了锯木厂,提供当地就业。 1975年共产党接管南越后,政府与宗教机构的关系发生了重大变化.

全国各地的教会财产受到越来越多的国家控制,宗教社区往往失去获得其以前拥有的土地和建筑物的机会。 救赎者坚持认为,他们从未自愿放弃对L ' Accueil财产的权利。

他们承认教会在1978年将与锯木厂有关的资产转移到了国家,但辩称转让不包括土地本身. 当局随后将财产分配给政府控制的机构。 其余部分占地约2,550平方米,目前由当地体育职业学校管理.

最近的努力 自1994年以来,教会一直要求归还财产。 它最近于10月24日向胡瓦克人民委员会提出正式申诉,要求承认其土地使用权并澄清财产的法律地位。 据报告,当局在11月8日的答复中驳回了申诉,称申诉没有审议依据。

10月在该地产张贴了一份通知,宣布计划在该地开发一个公共公园和停车场. 地方当局捍卫该项目是为了公共利益,包括在人口稠密地区改善交通条件和提供更多的绿色空间。 越南法律规定,土地属于人民集体所有,由国家管理。

政府当局还援引了2003年国民议会的一项决议,该决议一般禁止重新审议1991年7月1日之前确定的某些土地和住房安排。 但救赎者质疑政府对该地产历史的解释,

他们要求官员公开公布支持其决定的文件,并审查教会提出的历史记录。 争议说明了宗教共产主义的困难

summary: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a…   The post  Trump, Xi, and Putin Meet Amid Deteriorating Religious Freedom Conditions   first appeared on  Intern
summary_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但对面临的冲突和国际问题却很少提出具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了一个. .
title_zh: 特朗普、习近平和普京在宗教自由状况恶化之际会晤
content: U.S. President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin met Thursday in Shenzhen, China, for an unprecedented trilateral summit, projecting an image of cooperation among three of the world’s most powerful nations but offering few concrete agreements on the conflicts and international issues facing them. The roughly 80-minute meeting produced a joint statement addressing United Nations reform, energy production, international legal authority, and nuclear risks. However, the statement offered no clear breakthroughs on the wars in Ukraine or Iran and made no public reference to religious freedom or the persecution of religious communities in China and Russia. The gathering underscored the importance of direct engagement among world leaders as they seek to manage competing interests, global conflicts, and questions about the future of international order. The summit also offered an opportunity to address concerns affecting millions of people who face persecution for their faith, particularly in countries governed by authoritarian regimes. A Summit Focused on Global Stability The three leaders presented themselves as sharing responsibility for maintaining international peace and security. Their joint statement called for United Nations reform, increased production and supply of petroleum products, and further dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The leaders also emphasized state sovereignty and the immunity of government officials, declaring that the International Criminal Court and similar bodies should not abuse their authority. The language reflects a shared interest among the three governments in limiting the reach of international institutions, although their respective political, economic, and security priorities remain distinct. Concerningly, this language is similar to that used by China in pushing back on American calls to respect human rights and ensure citizens can freely practice religion. Claiming that these are internal affairs, China rejects what it considers to be overly zealous policing by the U.S. and continues on its path of persecution. Putin described the summit as a new chapter in diplomatic history and praised the opportunity for direct engagement with Trump and Xi. The Russian president also invoked the 1945 Yalta Conference, which helped shape the postwar European order, arguing that international conflicts eventually require countries to recognize realities on the ground. While the leaders expressed interest in dialogue and international stability, their meeting did not produce publicly announced agreements to resolve major conflicts or address underlying tensions between their governments. Religious Freedom Remains a Global Concern For religious freedom advocates, high-level diplomatic meetings represent an important opportunity to raise the plight of prisoners of conscience and religious communities facing government persecution. China, in particular, continues to impose severe restrictions on religious practice. Christians in unregistered churches face surveillance, detention, church closures, and pressure to submit to government oversight. The Chinese Communist Party’s campaign to bring religious institutions under its control has affected Protestant house churches, Catholic communities, Tibetan Buddhists, Uyghur Muslims, and other religious minorities. In recent months, international advocates have urged the Trump administration to raise the cases of imprisoned religious leaders with Xi. Earlier this year, Trump raised the case of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of Beijing’s Zion Church, during a meeting with Xi. Chinese authorities subsequently released Jin, who later relocated to the United States. However, other Zion Church leaders arrested during the same crackdown remain detained, and no such direct advocacy seems to have occurred at this most recent meeting. The case demonstrated how direct presidential engagement can potentially influence the circumstances
content_zh:
美国总统唐纳德·特朗普,中国国家主席习近平,俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京星期四在中国深圳举行前所未有的三边峰会,展现出世界三大强国之间合作的形象,但很少就它们面临的冲突和国际问题达成具体协议.

大约80分钟的会议产生了关于联合国改革、能源生产、国际法律权威和核风险的联合声明。 然而,该声明对于乌克兰或伊朗的战争没有提出明确的突破,也没有公开提及中国和俄罗斯的宗教自由或对宗教团体的迫害.

会议强调了世界领导人直接参与的重要性,因为他们寻求管理相互竞争的利益、全球冲突和有关国际秩序未来的问题。 首脑会议还提供了一个机会,解决影响到数百万因信仰而面临迫害的人的关切,特别是在专制政权统治的国家。

以全球稳定为重点的首脑会议 三位领导人自称分担维护国际和平与安全的责任。 他们的联合声明呼吁联合国改革、增加石油产品的生产和供应,以及就减少核风险进一步进行对话。

各国领导人还强调国家主权和政府官员的豁免权,宣布国际刑事法院和类似机构不应滥用其权力。 其措辞反映了三国政府对限制国际机构的影响力的共同利益,尽管它们各自的政治、经济和安全优先事项仍然不同。

关于这一点,这种语言类似于中国在抵制美国尊重人权和确保公民可以自由信奉宗教的呼声时所使用的语言。 中国声称这是内政,反对美国过于狂热地维持治安,继续走迫害的道路。

普京将峰会描述为外交史上的新篇章,并称赞与特朗普和习近平直接接触的机会. 俄罗斯总统还援引了1945年雅尔塔会议,会议帮助塑造了战后的欧洲秩序,认为国际冲突最终需要各国承认当地的实际情况.

虽然领导人对对话和国际稳定表示兴趣,但他们的会议没有达成公开宣布的协议,以解决重大冲突或解决政府之间的紧张关系。

宗教自由仍然是全球关注的问题 对于宗教自由倡导者来说,高级别外交会议是一个重要的机会,可以提高良心犯和宗教界面临政府迫害的困境。 特别是中国继续严格限制宗教活动.

在未登记的教堂的基督徒面临监视,拘留,教堂关闭,以及服从政府监督的压力. 中国共产党将宗教机构置于其控制之下的运动影响了新教住宅教堂,天主教社区,藏传佛教,维吾尔穆斯林等宗教少数派.

最近几个月,国际倡导者敦促特朗普政府向习近平提出被囚禁宗教领袖的案件. 今年早些时候,特朗普在北京锡安教会创始人伊兹拉·金明里牧师会见习近平时提出这个案例. 中国当局随后释放了后来移居美国的金.

然而,在同一次镇压中被捕的其他锡安教会领导人仍然被拘留,在最近的这次会议上似乎没有进行这种直接的宣传。 该案表明,总统直接参与会如何影响局势

summary_zh:
东南亚领导人在11月15日于马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟(东盟)峰会上重申反对缅甸军政府,认为缅甸的军事领导人在结束该国内战方面没有取得足够的进展后,延长了对该国政治代表权的限制.

这一决定是作为11名成员的领导人作出的... 在持续冲突期间,
title_zh: 在持续冲突的背景下，东盟继续将缅甸军政府排除在外
content: Southeast Asian leaders reaffirmed their opposition to Myanmar’s military government at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on Nov. 15, extending restrictions on the country’s political representation after concluding that its military leadership had made insufficient progress toward ending the country’s civil war. The decision came as leaders from the 11-member regional bloc gathered in the Philippines for three days of discussions on international conflicts, regional security, and economic stability. Myanmar’s continuing violence and humanitarian crisis featured prominently, alongside disputes in the South China Sea and the broader consequences of conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine. In a statement following their review of Myanmar’s implementation of a five-point peace plan adopted in 2021, ASEAN leaders expressed deep concern over the continuing conflict. They denounced attacks against civilians and public infrastructure. They called on all parties to halt indiscriminate violence, protect civilian populations, and allow humanitarian assistance to reach those in need. The leaders also agreed to maintain the restriction preventing Myanmar’s military leader and foreign minister from attending ASEAN summits and foreign ministers’ meetings until meaningful progress is made toward implementing the peace plan. Myanmar will continue to be represented at those meetings by lower-level diplomatic officials. The decision represents a positive continuation of ASEAN’s effort to pressure Myanmar’s military leadership while preserving diplomatic channels with the country. A Peace Plan with Little Progress Myanmar has been embroiled in a nationwide civil war since February 2021, when the military overthrew the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi. The coup prompted widespread protests and a violent crackdown by security forces. Armed resistance subsequently emerged across the country, with longstanding ethnic armed organizations also intensifying their campaigns against the military. In April 2021, ASEAN developed a five-point consensus intended to address the crisis. The agreement called for an immediate cessation of violence, constructive dialogue among all parties, mediation by an ASEAN special envoy, humanitarian assistance, and engagement between the envoy and relevant stakeholders. Despite repeated diplomatic efforts, the plan has produced little meaningful progress toward ending the conflict. ASEAN has struggled to balance its traditional policy of noninterference in member states’ domestic affairs with the need to respond to the increasingly severe humanitarian and political crisis in Myanmar. The bloc has maintained contact with the military government while withholding full political recognition at its highest-level meetings. In May 2025, ASEAN attempted to strengthen its approach by making the special envoy position permanent rather than replacing the representative annually. The change was intended to provide greater continuity in diplomatic engagement and improve the prospects for negotiations. However, continued military operations and widespread abuses have undermined those efforts. According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent monitoring organization, more than 8,600 people had been killed and 32,406 arrested by Myanmar’s security forces as of this week. The figures reflect the extensive human cost of the conflict and the government’s continued repression of opposition. Myanmar’s military leadership has also attempted to restore its international standing. Military chief Min Aung Hlaing became president in April following elections conducted in phases in December and January. Opposition groups and international observers criticized the elections as an effort to consolidate military control rather than restore genuine civilian government. Despite visits to several ASEAN member states, Min Aung Hlaing remains excluded from the bloc’s highest-level politi
content_zh:
东南亚领导人在11月15日于马尼拉举行的东南亚国家联盟(东盟)首脑会议上重申反对缅甸军政府,认为缅甸的军事领导在结束该国内战方面进展不足后,延长了对该国政治代表权的限制.

这项决定是11个成员的区域集团领导人在菲律宾聚集一堂,讨论国际冲突、区域安全和经济稳定问题,为期三天。 缅甸的持续暴力和人道主义危机与南中国海的争端以及中东和乌克兰冲突的更广泛后果一道,占据了显著地位。

东盟领导人在审查缅甸执行2021年通过的五点和平计划后发表声明,对持续冲突深表关切. 他们谴责对平民和公共基础设施的袭击。 他们呼吁所有各方停止不分青红皂白的暴力,保护平民,允许人道主义援助送达需要援助的人。

领导人还同意继续限制缅甸的军事领导人和外交部长出席东盟首脑会议和外交部长会议,直到在执行和平计划方面取得有意义的进展。 缅甸将继续派低级外交官员出席这些会议。

这一决定是东盟在保持与缅甸的外交渠道的同时向缅甸军事领导人施压的努力的积极继续。 自2021年2月军方推翻昂山素季当选政府以来,与小进步缅甸的和平计划卷入全国内战.

政变引发了广泛的抗议和安全部队的暴力镇压. 武装抵抗随后在全国各地出现,长期存在的族裔武装组织也加强了对军队的进攻。 2021年4月,东盟达成了旨在应对危机的五点共识.

协定要求立即停止暴力,所有各方进行建设性对话,由东盟特使进行调解,提供人道主义援助,特使与相关利益攸关方进行接触。 尽管一再作出外交努力,但该计划在结束冲突方面没有取得什么有意义的进展。

东盟努力在不干涉成员国内政的传统政策与应对缅甸日益严重的人道主义和政治危机的必要性之间取得平衡。 该集团与军政府保持联系,同时拒绝在最高级别会议上给予充分的政治承认。

2025年5月,东盟试图加强其做法,使特使的职位永久化,而不是每年更换代表。 这一变化旨在增加外交接触的连续性,改善谈判前景。 然而,持续的军事行动和普遍的侵权行为破坏了这些努力。

据独立监督组织政治犯援助协会称,截至本周,缅甸安全部队已杀害8 600多人,逮捕32 406人。 这些数字反映了冲突给人带来的巨大代价以及政府继续镇压反对派。

缅甸的军事领导人也试图恢复其国际地位。 在12月和1月分阶段举行选举之后,军事长官敏昂·赫莱于4月成为总统。 反对派团体和国际观察员批评选举是为了巩固军事控制而不是恢复真正的文职政府。

尽管访问了东盟的几个成员国,敏昂莱仍然被排除在集团最高领导层之外。

title: Fulani Militants Kill 14 Christians in Plateau State, Nigeria
summary: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure
summary_zh: 在尼日利亚博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统就其未能保护人民免受袭击一事呼吁原谅的几天后，在高原州的四个地方政府辖区内发生的最新袭击中，至少有14名基督徒被杀害。
title_zh: 富拉尼武装分子在尼日利亚高原州杀害14名基督徒
content: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure to visit violence-affected communities during an earlier trip to the state and promised to rebuild destroyed communities and return internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes. The killings occurred between Sunday, Nov. 15, and Monday, Nov. 16, in Mangu, Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos local government areas, according to community sources and local security groups. Armed attackers reportedly targeted rural settlements and ambushed residents traveling between communities. The latest violence followed Tinubu’s visit to Jos on Saturday, Nov. 14, for an All Progressives Congress (APC) political rally at Zaria Road Stadium, where he acknowledged the suffering of communities affected by recurring attacks and displacement. Addressing residents and party supporters, Tinubu asked Plateau residents to forgive him for not visiting affected communities during his previous trip to the state in April. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport,” he said. “Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation. I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.” The president promised to rebuild communities destroyed by violence and facilitate the return of displaced residents. “We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” Tinbu added. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.” He also commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, for identifying vulnerable populations and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Tinubu announced that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and that surveillance cameras promised to Plateau state had been procured to strengthen security monitoring and early warning operations. However, fresh attacks were reported within hours of the president’s departure from the state. In Mangu Local Government Area, armed attackers invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, killing nine people. Other residents were reportedly missing following the attack. Silas Nanfwang, a resident who confirmed the incident to journalists, called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate the attackers and bring those responsible to justice. In Barkin Ladi, 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos was killed when armed men invaded Sho village at about 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, according to the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM). The association’s National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, also reported the killing of 42-year-old Dauda John Davou during an attack on the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, at about 2 a.m. on Sunday. Another attack was reported in the Jol community around 12:10 a.m. on Sunday. According to BYM, local vigilantes responded to the attackers, preventing further casualties. The association said the incidents followed the shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol on Wednesday. He is currently receiving medical attention. BYM also reported that Ina Arin was killed when armed men ambushed him and his friend, Abok Gyang, as they returned to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang survived the attack. In Bokkos Local Government Area, two people, including a unit commander of the Plateau state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, were killed in an ambush on Monday afternoon. The victims, identified as Gambo and his companion, were traveling on a motorcycle from Hurti village to Tadai in Manguna District when armed men attacked them at about 1:30 p.m. They had reportedly visited Hurti for a condolence visit and died at the scene. Gambo had recently completed a refresher training program for Operation Rainbow unit commanders in Jos and was known amon

在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统呼吁原谅他在早些时候访问受暴力影响的社区,并承诺重建被摧毁的社区并让境内流离失所者返回其祖传家园几天后,在尼日利亚高原州四个地方政府地区,至少有14名基督徒被杀死。

据社区人士和地方安全团体称,这些杀戮发生在11月15日星期日至16日星期一的Mangu、Riyom、Barkin Ladi和Bokkos地方政府地区。 据报告,武装袭击者以农村定居点为目标,并伏击社区之间的居民。 在Tinubu于11月星期六访问Jos后,

14,在Zaria Road体育场举行全体进步人士大会(APC)政治集会,他承认一再受攻击和流离失所影响的社区遭受苦难。 蒂努布针对居民和政党支持者,要求高原居民原谅他4月前去该州旅行期间没有访问受影响的社区.

他说,“上次访问时,我仅限于机场。” “对不起,如果你没有在内地看到我,但我看到了灾难。 我收到州长的报告了 我在我国人民的脸上看到了恐怖。” 总统承诺重建被暴力摧毁的社区并便利流离失所居民回返。

Tinbu补充说,“我们将重建你们的社区,并将你们带回你们的社区。” “我已指示所有安全机构采取果断行动,并维持高原的和平与稳定。” 他还赞扬人道主义事务和减贫部长贝尔纳·多罗博士确定弱势人口和协调人道主义援助。

蒂努布宣布有1000名森林警卫正在接受训练,并且已经采购了向高原州承诺的监视相机,以加强安全监测和预警行动. 然而,据报道,总统离开国家后的数小时内又有新的袭击.

在Mangu地方政府地区,武装袭击者于星期日下午9时左右入侵Jipal区的Zwagal社区,造成9人死亡。 据报告,其他居民在袭击后失踪。 向记者证实此事的居民Silas Nanfwang呼吁安全机构加紧努力找到袭击者,并将责任人绳之以法。

在Barkin Ladi,79岁的Da Ishaku Pam Vwos被武装分子于星期日下午5:20左右入侵Sho村而死,据Berom青年穆尔德斯协会(BYM)称. 该协会的全国宣传秘书Rwang Tengwong还报道了42岁的Dauda John Davou星期天凌晨2时左右在Riyom LGA的Hoss区被Sambak社区袭击时被杀死的事件。

据报道,乔尔社区在星期日12:10左右又发生了一起袭击事件. 据BYM称,当地民团对袭击者作出反应,防止了进一步的伤亡. 该协会说,事件发生在周三Joshua Doro Dafwel被枪击后。 他目前正在接受治疗。

BYM还报告说,Ina Arin被武装分子伏击并被其朋友Abok Gyang杀死,当时他们返回了Foron区的多龙村。 克阳幸免于袭. 在博克科斯地方政府地区,包括高原国有保安装备"彩虹行动"的一名分队指挥官在内的两人于星期一下午被伏击而身亡.

受害者被确认为Gambo和他的同伴,他们乘坐摩托车从Hurti村前往Manguna区的Tadai,武装人员于下午1时30分左右袭击他们。 据报告,他们前往Hurti慰问,并在现场死亡。 甘博最近完成了 " 彩虹行动 " 部队指挥官在乔斯的进修培训方案,并被称作 " 阿蒙 "

title_zh: 女性可以成为执事吗？
content: ABSTRACT: Whether or not women can serve as deacons is a live question for many Christians, especially with more churches shifting from a deacon-led to an elder-led polity. The nature of the role, the example of Phoebe, and the qualifications for deacons in 1 Timothy 3 may allow room for deaconesses, but each of these arguments faces compelling counterarguments. In the absence of clear biblical evidence for women holding this formal office, wisdom leads Christians to approach the question with both conviction and charity. For our ongoing series of feature articles for pastors and Christian leaders, we asked Benjamin Merkle (PhD, The Southern Baptist Theological Seminary), Research Professor of New Testament and Greek at Southeastern Baptist Theological Seminary, to examine the biblical evidence for women serving as deacons. By asking the question “Can women serve as deacons?” we are not simply asking whether women can serve the church. Scripture obviously permits and commends women serving the church. The question is whether the New Testament permits women to hold the formal office of deacon. Many churches are asking this question, for at least two reasons. First, women should not be restricted from serving in places where the Bible does not restrict them. If the Bible permits women to be deacons, then a church’s tradition does not offer sufficient grounds to prohibit them from holding the office. Women are essential to the health and vitality of the church, and we certainly don’t want to limit the church’s effectiveness over an unbiblical practice. Second, many churches either have moved or are moving to a plural-eldership model of church leadership. Historically, many Baptist, baptistic, or nondenominational churches were governed by a board of deacons. These deacons held leadership authority in a way that many believe is inappropriate for the office of deacon. For complementarians, it would not be wise for women to be deacons in such a context since it would violate 1 Timothy 2:12 (“I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man”). Under complementarianism, the relevant question is not whether an office possesses any authority whatsoever, but whether an office’s authority constitutes the kind of teaching or governing authority restricted to men. If a deacon holds elder-like authority, then, regardless of the title used, it would be wrong for a woman to hold the position because she would have authority over a man. If, however, a church has male elders who have authority to lead the church, then some are asking if it would be permissible to allow women to be deacons since a deacon is a position with little to no authority. With hundreds of churches shifting from a deacon-led to an elder-led polity, the question of whether women can be deacons becomes relevant. This essay unfolds as follows. I present the three best views for allowing women to be deacons. 1 (I assume a complementarian framework. The egalitarian-versus-complementarian debate is important, but I will not address it here.) After presenting each argument in favor of women deacons, I provide counterarguments. Although there are reasonable arguments for allowing women to serve as deacons, this essay argues that the New Testament provides no clear text that permits women to hold the office of deacon. I conclude the essay with three principles to keep in mind when dealing with this issue in the local church. Argument 1: The Nature of the Office The first argument for allowing women to hold the office of deacon concerns the nature of the office itself: Deacons are servants and not leaders. 2 As servants, deacons do not possess authority but serve the church in low-key (though important) ways. Consequently, nothing in Scripture would prohibit women from holding this office. The elders (also called “overseers” or “pastors”) are given the task of teaching and leading the church. When comparing the qualifications for elders and deacons in 1 Timothy 3

ABSTRACT:妇女是否可以担任执事是许多基督徒的活生生的问题,特别是更多的教会从执事转向长者领导的政体。 角色的性质,菲比的例子,以及1 Timothy 3中的执事资格,可能为执事留有余地,但这些论点都面临着令人信服的反驳.

在没有明确的圣经证据证明妇女担任这一正式职务的情况下,智慧促使基督教徒以信念和慈善的态度对待这个问题。

对于我们目前为牧师和基督教领袖发表的一系列专题文章,我们请本杰明·梅尔克勒(PhD, The Southern Baptist Theocational Seminary),新约研究教授和东南浸信会神学院的希腊人,为担任执事的妇女审查圣经证据.

通过问“妇女能否担任执事?” 我们不仅仅是问妇女是否能够为教会服务。 圣经显然允许和赞扬为教会服务的妇女。 问题是新约是否允许妇女担任正式执事职务. 许多教会提出这个问题,至少有两个原因。

第一,不应限制妇女在圣经没有限制的地方服务。 如果《圣经》允许妇女担任执事,那么教会的传统就不足以禁止她们担任公职。 女性对教会的健康与活力至关重要,

第二,许多教堂要么已经搬迁,要么正在转向教会领导的多元-老年模式。 历史上,许多浸信会,洗礼会,或非宗派教会都由执事委员会管理. 这些执事以许多人认为不适合执事办公室的方式掌握领导权.

对于辅助者来说,在这样的背景下由妇女担任执事是不明智的,因为这将违反1 Timothy 2:12(“我不允许妇女教授或对男子行使权力”)。

在补充主义下,相关问题不是办公室是否拥有任何权威,而是办公室的权威是否构成仅限于男性的教学或管理权威。 如果执事拥有长者般的权威,那么,不管使用的头衔如何,女性担任这一职务是错误的,因为她将对男性拥有权威.

但是,如果一个教会有男性长者有权领导教会,那么有些人会问是否允许妇女担任执事,因为执事是一个几乎没有权力或没有权力的职位。 随着数百个教堂从执事转向长者领导的政体,妇女是否可以担任执事的问题变得重要. 这篇散文展开如下.

我提出三种最佳观点,允许妇女担任执事。 1(我假设是一个补充框架。) 平等与互补的辩论很重要,但我不想在这里谈论。 ) 在提出每一个有利于女性执事的论据后,我提出反驳.

虽然有合理的理由允许女性担任执事,但是这篇文章认为,新约没有给出允许女性担任执事的明确文本. 最后,我提出三项原则,以便在当地教会处理这一问题时铭记这些原则。

论点1:办公室的性质 允许妇女担任执事职位的第一个论点涉及办公室本身的性质:执事是仆人而不是领导者。 2个 作为仆人,执事并不拥有权威,而是以低调(虽然重要)的方式为教会服务. 因此,《圣经》中没有任何内容禁止妇女担任这一职务。

content: Audio Transcript Welcome back to the podcast on this Thanksgiving week. Yesterday, we read about Jesus washing the feet of his disciples in John 13. Jesus worked his basin of water from disciple to disciple on the floor. When he reached Peter, Peter instinctively pulled his feet back and said, “You shall never wash my feet.” Then “Jesus answered him, ‘If I do not wash you, you have no share with me.’ Simon Peter said to him, ‘Lord, not my feet only but also my hands and my head!’” Dump the basin on my head. Give me a shower! And then “Jesus said to him, ‘The one who has bathed does not need to wash, except for his feet, but is completely clean. And you are clean’” (John 13:8–10). Peter is clean. He was chosen, and he was redeemed. Christ’s future work has already applied to him. Now he only needs his feet washed. Confessing sin is a part of daily cleansing (1 John 1:9), and that practice is never inconsistent with being “completely clean.” Peter is a living metaphor for justification and sanctification. And it tells me we can miss what Christ has done for us because we have dirt on our feet. We fixate on washing off the dust every day. We obsess over daily sanctification and forget that Christ washed us clean. Today on Ask Pastor John: how to beat scrupulosity. Today’s question is from a middle-aged man named Dave. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question. I have struggled for many years with scrupulosity. That’s the word I learned last week while watching YouTube videos. When I looked up that word, scrupulosity, I wept for joy. My obsessive fears have destroyed my peace for many years. And I think I have discovered the root of most of my spiritual challenges and struggle with anxiety. So, now I want to ask you, Pastor John, what advice would you give to a man who has for years been paralyzed by scrupulosity?” There is a similarity between ordinary spiritual attacks that every believer endures, on the one hand, and more sustained obsessions that some believers endure, on the other hand. There’s a similarity. There’s an overlap. In other words, I don’t think we should overstate or understate the peculiar seriousness of what it is to deal with scrupulosity, or what is sometimes called obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD). Let me try to illustrate what I mean by the overlap between (1) the normal threat of a thought or an image or a behavior becoming an obsession that all of us experience and (2) the more persistent thoughts or images or behaviors that keep returning and returning, and won’t let a person have any rest, like a tick that bites you on the leg and sinks into your skin, and you try to pull it off, but it just grabs on deeper and harder. All of us deal with this danger. I’ve dealt with it personally and written about it, mostly in relation to sexual threats. For example, you inadvertently see some sexually riveting situation — say, a couple having sex on the ground behind your garage. Immediately, that image lodges itself in your consciousness with tremendous force. It threatens to take over. It wants to stay there and be developed in living color by your imagination. You can adapt this situation, this sexual temptation, to whatever your temptation is, whatever the threat of repetition is. You know the kind of thing I’m talking about. What do you do? Here’s my strategy. I’ll just sum it up quickly and then show how it might apply to this issue of scrupulosity. ANTHEM is my technique for handling a situation of threatening preoccupation with thoughts that ought not to be in my head. A: Avoid what triggers the thought or the image. If it’s inadvertent, don’t look back. If you can avoid the trigger in the first place, avoid it. N: Say no out loud to Satan, to your own mind. No — a strong, decisive no. “You will not have dominion over me (Romans 6:14)!” No to that thought, image, or memory. T: Turn your mind to another compelling reality. content: How often does church-leadership content online reveal a lightly veiled obsession with new ? The experts today might not come out and say it, but the assumption often seems to be: Surely after two thousand years and all of our light-year advances in technology, the church needs a serious upgrade. Capturing this sentiment, one article insists, “Church leaders face two options. Either battle the marketplace currents and strive to convince enough people to pay for sermon-centric Sunday gatherings, or rethink that model to better fit the realities of making disciples in the twenty-first century.” Someone recently shared a clip with me that illustrates one such updated model. The video features a popular preacher who begins his Sunday sermon by driving a Rolls-Royce onto a stage. Twenty-two screens surround him, and hundreds of light bulbs hang overhead. The “preacher” steps out of the half-a-million-dollar car and takes critics like me head-on: There are some of you who are saying, “Oh man, I can’t believe you drove a Rolls-Royce into church. Man, that’s gimmicky.” No, it’s not; it’s godly. “Oh, that’s trite. That’s flippant.” No, it’s from Christ’s playbook. If you ever go to church and you find yourself bored, blame the communicator, the pastor. Don’t blame God. Yeah, for some reason we go to church and expect boredom. Just the opposite should be true. We are — and this is going to mess you up — we are in the entertainment business. I agree that no one should be bored in church — and I certainly agree that God is not to blame for any boredom in the pews. This preacher’s gimmick implies, however, that the same old formula for church — prayer, singing, fellowship, preaching — can’t possibly keep the attention of modern people like you. Mere sermons won’t cut it. God needs us to spice things up. God is not surprised by our state-of-the-art technology or shriveling attention spans, and he has told us, from the beginning, what captures souls when we gather for worship. He’s told us how to do church, and his counsel hasn’t expired. A Church Anyone Would Want Do you want to hear about a church that was emphatically not bored? They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers. And awe came upon every soul , and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles. And all who believed were together and had all things in common. And they were selling their possessions and belongings and distributing the proceeds to all, as any had need. And day by day, attending the temple together and breaking bread in their homes, they received their food with glad and generous hearts, praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved. (Acts 2:42–47) Don’t you want to be a part of a church like that? Don’t you want your local church to taste the camaraderie, sacrifice, growth, and joy these people experienced when they gathered? The God-authored recipe is remarkably simple and durable: “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” What did this church do when it grew so wildly and unexpectedly? They gathered. They ate. They gave. They prayed. They preached. And because they devoted themselves to God’s inspired Sunday-service plan, they rejoiced and their numbers multiplied. It’s dumbfounding that we see this kind of church thrive for literally millennia and still conclude it’s time to shake things up. “Sunday sermons got us this far,” we say, “but we’ll take it from here.” What if God knew everything we know — artificial intelligence, fiber-optic internet, driverless cars, those new robot vacuums that can clean stairs — and deliberately told churches to pray, sing, eat, drink, and preach the word anyway? Preaching to Itching Ears God knew exactly what changes and pressures our churches would face in the twenty-first century, and so he warned us t

title_zh: 神圣的盛宴让饕餮之徒望洋兴叹
content: It’s feasting season. Thanksgiving. Advent. New Year’s. But for Americans in particular, is there such a thing as a non -feasting season? Our society has a bizarre love-hate relationship with food, pulling the plate toward us with one hand while pushing it away with the other. On the one hand, about 40 percent of adults are clinically obese; on the other, more than one in eight adults rely on GLP-1 to suppress their appetite. We want food and we want to want food less. We struggle to break free from the clutches of Big Food, so we look to Big Pharma for help. Happy Thanksgiving? What’s the remedy for this gastronomic schizophrenia? As counterintuitive as it sounds, godly feasting provides an antidote to foolish gluttony. Feasting vs. Feeding The Bible has a lot to say about food, not just in isolated verses but in plot points central to the arc of Scripture. Many of the most egregious sins centered on food. For instance, the first sin involved rebellious eating, looking to something forbidden in search of goodness (Genesis 3:6). After the exodus, Israel grumbled about their desire for Pharaoh’s pots of meat (Exodus 16:3). Then, when the Lord provided manna in the wilderness, Israel reenacted the sin of Eve when they gathered food on the Sabbath against God’s command (Exodus 16:27–30). But the Bible also commends feasting, both spiritual and physical. Jesus offers himself as the bread of life, given for the nourishment of the saints in exile (John 6:35). And the church looks forward to a meal at the consummation of history, the marriage feast of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). Between the resurrection and return of the Lamb, we weekly feast on his body and blood, anchoring our minds on what Christ has done and what Christ will do (1 Corinthians 11:23–26). Godly feasting leans into our place in between the times by remembering with gratitude what was and anticipating with joy what will be. All the blessed feasts in the Scriptures are communal celebrations . Something extraordinary has happened; raise a glass to the King! We shouldn’t eat what we regularly eat today; instead, “bring the fattened calf and kill it, and let us eat and celebrate. For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found!” (Luke 15:23–24). We break from feeding ourselves (simply giving our body what it needs) in order to feast (eating and drinking more than we need) as a blessed means of joyously celebrating the work of God in history. But most Christians rarely, if ever, truly feast with mindful gratitude. We just overeat. Spiritual Malnutrition “A companion of gluttons shames his father” (Proverbs 28:7). The glutton does not feast; his god is his belly. He looks for deliverance in his next snack, his next meal, his next drink. He does not fully grasp that man does not live by bread alone. He is not marked by gratitude. The emptiness in his soul, the purposelessness of his life, and the joylessness of his ease have taken root as a spiritual disease. “A glutton is one who raids the icebox for a cure for spiritual malnutrition,” Frederick Buechner observed ( Wishful Thinking , 35). Americans, overall, remain locked in a permanent state of pseudo-feasting. Our culture combines industrial-grade, highly addictive food products and dopamine-seeking, nihilistic joylessness. We mindlessly munch. Often, we hardly even taste or enjoy our food. (A 2026 JAMA study revealed 69 percent of kids and 78 percent of adults use screens while eating.) This is an often-undiscussed problem within the church. I don’t know any Christians who intend to be gluttonous. But I know many, myself included, who have at times felt buried by the shame that follows an episode or season marked by a lack of self-control. We know we cannot make peace with sin, but we aren’t sure what this specific path of repentance looks like. So, when believers recognize the shameful pattern, we try to restrict our calories or go on a diet, which doesn’t stick. We purge and we binge — godless,
