The Lottie Moon Christmas Offering® (LMCO) totaled $212.5 million to support International Mission Board (IMB) missionaries, and the Annie Armstrong Easter Offering® (AAEO) reached $73.6 million to support the North American Mission Board’s (NAMB) church planting, compassion ministry and other evangelistic efforts to reach North America. IMB President Paul Chitwood said he celebrates what God did in the 2025-26 season and what He is doing now to lead Southern Baptists toward historic generosity. “I thank God for Southern Baptists! With giving through the Lottie Moon offering at an all-time high, churches and individual givers continue to display a heart for the gospel to be proclaimed to every nation, all tribes, peoples and languages,” Chitwood said. The Annie total marked the second highest in NAMB’s history. The record Lottie Moon offering total surpassed last year’s total by more than $5 million and is the best offering in IMB history. “God is giving our generation unprecedented opportunity to send missionaries to the most unreached peoples and places,” Chitwood continued. “Though the challenges faced by our missionaries are enormous, the generosity of Southern Baptists ensures they have what they need to face those challenges and continue in the work while we hold the ropes with our support.” IMB missionary Landon Williams (center) walks with a Chilean pastor and a U.S. pastor on a remote island in Chile. Cooperation and generosity among Southern Baptists fuels the work to reach the uttermost parts of the world with the gospel. In response to the offering totals, Sandy Wisdom-Martin, executive director-treasurer of WMU, said: “As Southern Baptists, we are all in for His mission. When we give sacrificially, we prioritize the mission of God. Together our fervent prayers, our faithful generosity and our wholehearted obedience become channels for the gospel to reach our neighbors as well as the nations.” For the last 10 years, Southern Baptists have increasingly supported the Annie offering, setting records in seven of the last 10 years. Totals in each of the last four years have surpassed $70 million. “I am so grateful to the pastors and churches for the faithfulness and generosity they have demonstrated through this offering,” said NAMB president Kevin Ezell. “As I travel and speak in churches of all sizes, I love seeing the posters in the hallways showing their offering goals. For some it is a few hundred dollars, for others several thousand.” The Annie Armstrong offering supports more than 3,000 missionaries in North America, including the ongoing work of church planting in the U.S. and Canada. In 2025, Southern Baptists planted the largest number of churches, 699, since 2016. title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
summary_zh: 北中央省
title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.
content_zh:
2013年5月哈萨克斯坦逮捕Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev牧师时,他是一位老人。 指控是奇怪的,他伤害了一名教会成员的健康并煽动了宗教仇恨。 他们判处他十年监禁,并把他关进精神病病房,囚犯经常在那里服药。 进来的路上,他觉得这也许是他心智的终结.

"这可能是我最后一次在正确的思想中和你说话,"他说. 然后,一个问题来到他身上,神用的那种。 "你的信仰在哪里?" 在升起的上帝的掩护下 有东西解除了 "我觉得自己在升天主的掩护下,"他说. 期待失去自我的老人却发现耶稣比墙壁更靠近. 他开始和周围的人交谈

对一个吸毒成瘾的囚犯来说 他只是说 只有耶稣才能帮助你 里面有九个月,近一百名囚犯为基督献出了生命。 "在狱中",他说"圣灵为我打开了祈祷的一个维度". 打算打破他的地方成为了他一生中最有成果的支点. 他们于2014年初释放了他。

他走了出去 埋下了好消息 在最后的地方 没有人会寻找它。 上帝不会被任何锁住你的门锁住 他已经在里面等了

title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱

title: He survived the killing fields. Then he baptised the man who ran a death camp
summary: 🇰🇭Cambodia· 1980s-1990s
title_zh: 他从“杀戮之地”幸存下来。后来，他为一名曾经营死亡集中营的人施洗。
content: Christopher LaPel grew up near the royal palace in Cambodia and wore a small ivory cross as a boy, though his father disapproved. Then the Khmer Rouge came. In 1975 he was driven into the labour camps, working sixteen-hour days in the fields. He lost both parents, a brother, and a sister to execution and starvation. He nearly died himself. When he was too sick to work for three days, soldiers came to execute him, and one of them looked at him and said he really looks sick, and walked away. He survived into a refugee camp in Thailand, empty and grieving. There a missionary told him that Jesus Christ had died on the cross for his sins. "This is the answer I've been waiting for," LaPel said, and he gave Jesus his life. The general who said, my sin is so deep LaPel became a pastor and went back to teach his own people. In 1995 a quiet man calling himself Hang Pin came to one of his leadership trainings. He gave his life to Christ, was baptised the next day, and began leading a house church. Only later did the world learn who he really was. Kang Kek Iew, known as Comrade Duch, had run S-21, the prison where around twelve thousand people were tortured and killed. He came to LaPel and said, "My sin is so deep." Duch surrendered to the authorities and was sentenced to life in prison, where he wore out the Bibles LaPel kept sending him. The man who survived the killing fields carried the grace of Jesus back to one of the men who built them. No sin is too deep for the blood of Jesus. Not the worst thing done to you. Not the worst thing you have done.
content_zh:
克里斯托弗·拉佩尔(Christopher LaPel)在柬埔寨的皇家宫殿附近长大并作为一个男孩穿小象牙十字架,尽管他的父亲不赞成. 后来红色高棉来了. 1975年,他被驱入劳改营,在田地工作了16小时. 他的父母、兄弟和姐妹都死于处决和饥饿。 他差点死了

当他生病了三天不能工作时,士兵们来处决他,其中一人看着他,说他真的病了,走了. 他活了下来,进入了泰国的一个难民营,空虚而悲伤. 有一个传教士告诉他,耶稣基督因他的罪而死于十字架上. 拉佩尔说:"这就是我一直在等待的答案",他给了耶稣一命.

将军说,我的罪恶是如此之深拉佩尔成为牧师,回去教自己的人. 1995年,一个叫作"杭平"的安静人来到了自己的领导训练之一. 他把生命献给基督,第二天被洗礼,并开始领导一所房屋教堂. 直到后来,世界才知道他的真实身份.

姜克毅被称作"杜克同志",曾经营过S-21监狱,当时大约有一万二千人被拷打并杀害. 他来到拉佩尔说:"我的罪恶是如此之深". 杜克向当局自首并被判处终身监禁,在那里他穿了"圣经"LaPel继续送去.

在杀戮地中幸存下来的人将耶稣的恩典带回了建造他们的人之一. 没有罪过是太深 对于耶稣的血。 不是对你最坏的事 不是你做过的最坏的事

title: A witch doctor got a solar radio. It was tuned to the truth
summary: 🇨🇬Democratic Republic of Congo· 2010s
summary_zh: 🇨🇬刚果民主共和国·21世纪10年代
title_zh: 巫医有一台太阳能收音机。它被调到了真相频道
content: Mbutu was a witch doctor in a remote village in the Democratic Republic of Congo. For years he cast spells, claimed power over the natural world, and sold cures to sick villagers who had nowhere else to turn. People feared him. He made his living off that fear. Then he was given a small solar-powered radio. It was fixed to one station, a local Christian broadcast, and handed out to villagers who had no other way to hear anything. Tuned to the truth So Mbutu listened. Day after day the good news came through that little speaker. He learned of the One who really controls the universe, and more than that, he learned about the love of Jesus and His offer of forgiveness. The man who had traded in fear laid his witchcraft down and gave his life to Christ. He did not keep it to himself. Mbutu now walks from village to village, finding other witch doctors and telling them what he found. Some of them have become believers. Some have become pastors, planting churches where there were none. A cheap radio and the name of Jesus were enough to turn the most feared man in the village into its brightest light. No one is beyond the reach of that name. Not the person others are afraid of. Not you.
content_zh:
Mbutu是刚果民主共和国一个偏远村庄的一名巫医。 多年来,他施了咒语,声称对自然世界拥有权力,并出售给没有别处可转的病村民的治疗方法. 人们害怕他。 他靠恐惧为生 后被给予小型太阳能收音机.

它被固定在一个电台,一个当地的基督教广播,并交给没有其他办法听到任何消息的村民. 实话实说 姆博图听了 日复一日的好消息从那个小演讲者那里传来。 他得知了真正控制宇宙之人,不止于此,他还了解到了耶稣的爱和他提出的宽恕.

在恐惧中交易的人放下了巫术,将他的生命献给了基督. 他没有保守秘密。 姆布图现在从村到村走来走去,找到其他巫医,并告诉他们他发现了什么. 他们中有一部分已变成信士。 有些人成为牧师,在没有教堂的地方种植教堂。

一个廉价的收音机和耶稣的名字足以将村里最被敬畏的人变成最明亮的光芒. 没有人能够超越这个名字。 不是别人害怕的人 不是你,你没有

title_zh: 如果家庭游戏之夜能让您的孩子谈论圣经，会怎么样？
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Doxa Games . This post is written by Marco Bartholomae, founder of Doxa Games and creator of the Bible-based board and card games Trials & Triumphs , Bible Clash , and Hurry! Fleeing Disciples . A couple of years ago, I was playing cards with my kids when a question hit me. What would it take to make a Bible game they’d ask to play again? I grew up in Germany with four brothers. We played cards on long car rides and spent hours on our bedroom floor with a board game spread out between us. I still remember how easy it was to lose track of time when we played together. Now I live in California with my wife and our four children, and we still love a good game night. The screens go away, somebody wants a rematch, and we get to enjoy being together. That question from the card table stayed with me. I started imagining games that could give other families that same experience and get them talking about Scripture along the way, games a child could sit down to, learn the rules, and enjoy right away, even if they were new to the Bible. Then maybe a name on a card or something that happened on the board would make them curious enough to ask a question. That’s how Doxa Games started. The Conversations That Start Around the Table In Deuteronomy 6, God tells his people to speak about his commandments with their children as they go about ordinary life, including when they sit at home. A game night gives us another chance to do that. Our games don’t replace family devotions, but they do open conversations about God’s Word. Your child might pick up a card and ask who Thaddaeus was. A race to a house church might get them wondering why the early Christians gathered in homes. Those are questions you can follow right back to Scripture. That’s also why I chose the name Doxa . It’s the Greek word for glory . In 1 Corinthians 10:31, Paul reminds us to do everything to the glory of God, even in ordinary things like eating and drinking. That conviction shapes what we make and how we think about time around the table. Three Games to Play With Your Family Bible Clash: Gospels (ages 8+) is a fast-paced, head-to-head card game. Play characters from the four Gospels and try to outscore your opponent. Trials & Triumphs (ages 5+) sends players down a winding path where one turn can move you forward, and the next can set you back. It gives younger kids a way to talk about trusting Christ through trials. Hurry! Fleeing Disciples (ages 8+) takes you into the world of Acts. Choose your route, evade Roman guards, and race to reach a house church. From Our Family Table to the Mission Field As Doxa grows, we hope to translate these games and put them in the hands of missionaries, church planters, and ministry training centers in places like Colombia, the Philippines, and East Africa. I’d love for a family in Malawi to pull out one of these games, play it in their own language, and have the same kinds of conversations we have around our table. If your family is getting together this Christmas, pick a game, clear a spot at the table, and let the kids make the first move. See all three games at DoxaGames.com . 我们的游戏不会取代家庭奉献, 你的孩子可能会拿起一张卡 问Thaddaeus是谁 参加一个家庭教堂的比赛,他们可能会想知道为什么早期的基督徒聚集在家中. 这些是你们可以追寻到圣经的问题 也正因为如此, 这是希腊的荣耀之词。

在1科林斯10:31中,保罗提醒我们要为上帝的荣耀做一切事情,即使在普通的事物中,比如吃喝. 这种信念决定了我们所做的以及我们如何思考在座时间。 三款游戏"玩与你的家庭圣经碰撞:福音"(glass (ages 8+))是一款速度快,头对头的牌游戏. 扮演四个福音派的人物,并尝试超越对手.

我们希望能翻译这些游戏, 并交给哥伦比亚、菲律宾和东非等地的传教士、教会植树人和部委训练中心。

content: Good morning. Grace and peace to you. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include some devotional and daily liturgy books like Dane Ortlund’s In the Lord I Take Refuge: 150 Daily Devotions through the Psalms and Jonathan Gibson’s Be Thou My Vision: A Liturgy for Daily Worship . Westminster Books has put together a Christmas Gift Guide that has all kinds of great options for anyone on your Christmas list. Recommended Reading Your Riches Are Stored Up in Leonida. Dakota Fiebranz says that since it’s the easiest and most expected thing in the world to criticize Grand Theft Auto , he takes a different tack and writes about what its popularity says about its users. “For those unfamiliar with the Grand Theft Auto series, the premise is relatively simple. You’re placed in a fictional American city, usually in the character of a criminal, and given a staggering amount of freedom to carry out your most dubious ambitions. You can steal cars (as the name suggests), but you can also rob banks, shoot civilians, commit vehicular manslaughter, and flee arrest, all with few to no consequences. You are truly free in the world of crime.” Learn From Autistic People About Evangelism. “These days, I seem to know an awful lot about trains. Train companies, liveries and logos. I know about engines and carriages, railway lines, stations and routes. I don’t actually use the trains all that much nor am I any sort of train enthusiast; I don’t, and never have, had any great interest in trains. What I am, however, is the father of a very classically autistic teenage boy.” Stephen Kneale explains what we can learn about evangelism from people with autism. How to Fire Someone at a Christian Organization. Unfortunately, even Christian people working for Christian organizations sometimes need to be let go. This article offers wisdom for those times. “When we hold back the hard call, we tell ourselves a story about mercy: I don’t want to be the one who upends this person’s life, so I won’t go there. That’s a heavy burden to put on your shoulders. To believe you’re ruining someone’s life by ending his employment is to believe you hold his future in your hands. But here’s the thing: You don’t. You aren’t sovereign over this person’s story. You cannot see his next chapter. The assumption that you can, that keeping him in a role where he’s failing is protecting him from some fate only you can foresee, isn’t humility. It’s pride.” America Needs a New Temperance Agenda. Brad Littlejohn writes about the recent political earthquake in the U.S. and explains why America needs a new temperance agenda. “Our markets, rather than serving American families, are tearing them apart, and American voters are primed for leaders willing to rein in an economy that caters to appetite and impulse rather than genuine human needs. Rather than narrowing our moral message, it’s time to broaden it—and with it, our coalition.” Praise God From Whom All Sparrows Flow. Kevin Burrell explains how a bird told him that the season of gratitude has begun. “The mid-fall arrivals of fall colors and flannel and pumpkin spice lattes can trigger our hearts to a sort of Thanksgiving nostalgia; they announce, like my backyard sparrows, ‘Remember, ‘tis the season to give thanks!’ But if we let them, these annual bellwethers can slingshot us well past an afternoon of turkey and football and reciting a couple of blessings around the table.” The Housing Crisis and the Biblical Duty of Stewardship. This is a thoughtful piece about the housing crisis. The context is the U.S., but much of it applies to Canada as well. “If we want young Americans to have a genuine opportunity to build stable lives, it’s not enough to implement another temporary affordability program. We need to recover a vision of economic life rooted in stewardship and responsibility, with the goal of flourishing families.” Reader Recommendations Once a week, I like to ask what you enjoy and recommend. What books, products, videos, sites, or oth

而不是缩小我们的道德信息,现在应该扩大它,并随之扩大我们的联盟。 赞美上帝,从谁 所有麻雀流。 凯文·伯雷尔(Kevin Burrell)解释了一只鸟如何告诉他,感恩的季节已经开始了. “落叶彩色和香肠和南瓜香料拿铁的中途抵达者,可使我们的心灵触发某种感恩节怀旧;

content: It was a great honor to be able to partner with Missionary to create Goers , a series of illustrated biographies for children. Each biography introduces young readers and listeners to the stories of men and women who were sent by churches to spread the good news about Jesus Christ to the ends of the earth. Each is illustrated by the ultra-talented Rommel Ruiz. The books can be purchased as a set of three or as individual volumes. The Plowboy’s Bible: The Story of William Tyndale’s English Translation . Hunted by spies, William Tyndale fled across Europe with a bounty on his head, his Bible translation labeled as contraband. Young John, on the other hand, has a long day of farm work ahead of him. Although their lives seem worlds apart, John’s father knows a story that binds John and William together—their love for God’s word. The scripture John relies on for encouragement cost William everything, but they gave John’s family everything! Rescued from Darkness: Amy Carmichael and the Girls of Dohnavur . Kumari is scared, helpless, and alone in a dark temple until Amma, a mysterious woman from a faraway land, carries her away to a beautiful garden. This is not a fairy tale. It’s the true story of missionary Amy Carmichael and the children she rescued and raised at Dohnavur Fellowship in India. Into the Unknown: David Livingstone’s Heart for Africa . Before David Livingstone was the most famous man in the world, he was a boy who dreamed of being free to explore God’s creation. But when David reached the mission field, he found that freedom taken from the people he tried to teach about the Creator. This is the story of a goer’s dangerous journey to the ends of the earth, of his courageous stand for justice, and of his patient endurance for the sake of Christ. The Goers series is written for children ages 4–10, and is ideal for parents to read to their children or for young readers to read on their own. Each book includes discussion questions and prayer points to get your family thinking and praying about the Great Commission. Each hardcover volume has 40 full-color pages and is sized 10″ x 10″. The Goers series is currently available exclusively through Westminster Books . Look for three more volumes to be added to the series around this time next year. content_zh:
能够和传教士合作创作Goers, 每部传记都向年轻的读者和听众介绍被教会派去向世界末端传播耶稣基督的好消息的男女的故事. 每个都由超能的隆美尔·鲁伊斯(英语:Rommel Ruiz)来说明.

书籍可作为一套三卷或单卷购买. 《犁男孩的圣经:威廉·廷达勒英文译本的故事》。 在间谍的追捕下,威廉·廷达勒带着头上的赏金逃过欧洲,他的圣经译本标注为违禁品. 而年轻的约翰则有很长的一天的农场工作在他前面.

虽然他们的生活似乎有些不同,但约翰的父亲却知道一个把约翰和威廉联系在一起的故事——他们对上帝之言的爱。 圣经中约翰依靠的鼓励让威廉付出了一切,但他们给了约翰的家人一切! 从黑暗中拯救:艾米·卡迈克尔和多赫纳武尔的少女.

库马里害怕,无助,独自在黑暗的神庙中,直到远方的神秘女子阿玛把她带到美丽的花园. 这不是童话 这是传教士Amy Carmichael和在印度Dohnavur联谊会救起和抚养的孩子的真实故事。 David Livingstone的非洲之心。

在大卫·利文斯通(David Livingstone)是世界上最有名的人之前,他是一个梦想自由探索上帝创造的男孩. 但是当大卫到达任务领域时,他发现自由从那些他试图教导造物主的人身上夺走.

这是一位行者前往地球尽头的危险旅程,他勇敢地站在正义面前,以及他为基督而耐心忍耐的故事。 Goers系列为4–10岁的儿童写作,是父母向子女阅读或年轻读者自己阅读的理想.

每本书都包含讨论问题和祈祷点,以让你的家人思考和祈祷大委员会. 每个硬盖卷有40页全色,大小为10′′×10′′. Goers系列目前完全通过Westminster Books提供。 明年的这个时候再找三卷

content: Good morning. If you have read this site for any length of time, you will know that I am not the kind of person who does hot takes, since I just don’t trust myself to do them well. However, with the Wesley Huff situation developing, I did want to link to what I consider an especially helpful assessment of the matter. You can find that beneath today’s recommended reads. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several volumes in the excellent New Studies in Dogmatics series. You’ll also find books by Jinger Duggar Vuolo, David Mathis, John Piper, and others. I continue to find and highlight hardcover and softcover book deals as part of Amazon’s Pre-Black Friday Book Deals . There are around 80 of them now, many of which are half off or more. Recommended Reading Hot Water and Holy Wonder: Giving Thanks for Ordinary Luxuries. “Every now and then, as I sit in my home library, a sense of awe settles over me—a spirit of wonder at the everyday comforts that surround me.” Trevin Wax celebrates the joy of the ordinary luxuries that God so graciously grants us. Are My Prayers Selfish? Responding to a question from a listener, John Piper explains the difference between prayers that are selfish and those that simply ask for things. “James is saying there is a kind of prayer that treats God like a cuckold. It refers to a husband whose wife is cheating on him. That’s a cuckold. Christians are making God into a cuckold. How? When it says they are praying just to spend it on their passions. The picture is of an unfaithful wife who asked her husband for $50 so she can go down the hall and pay another man to have sex with her. That’s the picture. She’s using prayer to cheat on her husband, God.” When the Heavens Declare: What a Solar Halo Says to a Secular City. Johannesburg was recently the site of a solar halo ( see here for images ). Tim Cantrell writes about what the skies were declaring in that moment. Gospel-Pilling the Looksmaxxers: Hope for Despairing Men. “What do dating apps, the 1999 film The Matrix, rhinoplasty, crystal meth, and smashing your face with a hammer all have in common? Welcome to the world of looksmaxxers. Let’s start at the beginning.” Mark Sanders introduces a concerning trend for young men and offers a much more satisfying hope. Here Are the Lessons I’ve Learned About Single Missionaries (From a Lifetime of Being One). I’m neither single nor a missionary, but still very much appreciate Andy Smith’s thoughts on the matter. “I always assumed that I would get married. I never thought I would enter full-time ministry. Yet, here I am, a contented single missionary since 1989.” Don’t Be Afraid to Provoke Your Brothers. Michael Kelley says why it’s important that we provoke one another. “I grew up in a house with two brothers. By the time we were all in school, ‘provoking’ was down to an art form. For each of my brothers, I knew the right buttons to push to get a rise out of them. I knew the words, the facial expressions, or even the subtle hint to drop that would flush their anger. What’s more, I knew how to do it to one of them to get at the other one. Like I said, an art form.” On Wesley Huff All those who have heard the recent news about Wesley Huff’s plagiarism have been shocked by it, myself no less than anyone else. I think Glen Scrivener is especially helpful, firm, and compassionate in this video . Even if you don’t watch it all, consider watching the final 10 minutes for the brief “sermon” he preaches there. Huff released a statement yesterday, which you can read on X or Facebook . Flashback The Blessing of a Higher Purpose in Our Pain. The chief end of affliction is to glorify God and enjoy him. The purpose of our lives is the purpose of our times of struggle, loss, grief, illness, and bereavement. The local church enables the world to look upon the canvas of God’s people and see an authentic painting of Christ’s love and holiness, not a forgery. —Jonathan Leeman Download Share See Also A La Carte (September 18

content: I have been blogging at Challies.com on a daily basis for over 23 years now. That long commitment has allowed me to write thousands of articles and hundreds of book reviews while also sending millions of visitors to other sites through the daily A La Carte feature. Though I’ve also written a number of books, the blog has always remained the “main thing.” Much of the blog’s content is now also translated into Spanish , French , and a number of other languages. One of my great desires has always been to freely give away as much as possible. I intend for it to always remain entirely free for all who visit . While, for obvious reasons, this can’t happen when it comes to books, I’ve made it my goal to ensure that everything else has been freely and widely distributed. While this has been possible largely because of advertisers, there is also a key role for the generosity of individuals. This is where patrons come in—patrons like you. There are a couple of different options for you to consider. The first is recurring monthly gifts. A service called Patreon provides a convenient means of linking content producers (like me) with ongoing supporters (like you). You can learn more and sign up at Patreon.com/challies . I also share monthly ministry and family updates there. The second is one-time gifts. If that is of interest to you, they can be made electronically via PayPal . If you prefer to send a one-time gift via check, you can simply mail a check (drawn on a US or Canadian bank) to this address: Tim Challies 1011 Upper Middle Road East, Box #1214 Oakville, Ontario L6H 5Z9 Canada Funds donated will be used to support my family and to help create great content or to otherwise improve, support, and enhance Challies.com. In one way or another, they will all be used to allow me to continue to do what I have been doing for these past 23+ years. Please understand that I intend for Challies.com to always remain entirely free. In fact, patrons help ensure that it always remains that way. Thank you for considering becoming a patron of Challies.com. Your support means so much to me. And this is the end of my once-yearly mention of this subject! title: México abre un año de memoria y reconciliación a cien años de la Cristiada – Infovaticana Blogs
summary: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo
summary_zh: 墨西哥天主教会本周日将开启这一活动，其标志被设计为记忆的圣物盒，并发出号召，开始在各教区转化为具体安排。
title_zh: 墨西哥在克里斯蒂亚达百年之际开启纪念与和解之年——Infovaticana博客
content: Con un emblema concebido como relicario de la memoria y con convocatorias que comienzan a traducirse en disposiciones concretas dentro de las diócesis, la Iglesia católica en México abre este domingo 22 de noviembre el Año Jubilar por el centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. La celebración comenzará en la solemnidad de Jesucristo, Rey del Universo, y se prolongará hasta el 21 de noviembre de 2027. El Jubileo lleva como lema “Su fe, nuestra memoria y su testimonio, nuestra misión”. Su propósito no consiste únicamente en recordar los acontecimientos que sacudieron la vida religiosa del país entre 1926 y 1929, sino en recuperar el testimonio de los mártires, promover la reconciliación y reafirmar la libertad religiosa como un derecho de toda persona. La presentación del emblema oficial, presidido por la proclamación “¡Viva Cristo Rey!”, ofrece una síntesis visual de esa finalidad. El diseño adopta la forma de un medallón o relicario en cuyo interior aparecen la Iglesia y el pueblo congregados bajo Cristo Rey. La Virgen de Guadalupe, la Eucaristía radiante, las coronas real y de espinas, así como las figuras del clero, la vida consagrada, los jóvenes y los fieles laicos, articulan una composición construida alrededor de tres conceptos: fe, memoria y testimonio. El color guinda remite a la sangre derramada por los mártires y las estrellas evocan el manto de la Virgen de Guadalupe. El emblema, por tanto, no constituye solamente la identificación gráfica de una efeméride, pretende expresar la continuidad histórica de una experiencia religiosa y transmitirla a las generaciones que conocen la cristiada como un episodio cada vez más distante. El Año Jubilar fue anunciado el 9 de noviembre durante la misa de apertura de la CXXI Asamblea Plenaria de la Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano, celebrada en la Basílica de Guadalupe. En ese contexto, el obispo de Cuernavaca y presidente de la CEM, Ramón Castro, subrayó que recordar la persecución religiosa no significa reabrir heridas, alimentar resentimientos ni señalar enemigos. La memoria cristiana de la resistencia cristera, explicó el Episcopado, debe conducir al reconocimiento del sufrimiento, la reconciliación y la construcción de la paz. Esta precisión resulta indispensable para evitar que el centenario sea utilizado como exaltación de la violencia o como argumento para trasladar al presente las confrontaciones políticas y religiosas del pasado. El Jubileo cuenta con un decreto de la Penitenciaría Apostólica, fechado el 6 de noviembre de 2026, mediante el cual se concede indulgencia plenaria a los fieles que cumplan las condiciones establecidas por la Iglesia y peregrinen a los santuarios dedicados a los mártires mexicanos o a los templos jubilares designados por los obispos. La Conferencia del Episcopado Mexicano pidió que el decreto sea proclamado en las Iglesias particulares este 22 de noviembre y que cada diócesis disponga los lugares, celebraciones y actividades pastorales correspondientes. La apertura nacional comienza así a adquirir características propias en las comunidades diocesanas. Entre las convocatorias más amplias se encuentra la del arzobispo de Guadalajara, cardenal José Francisco Robles Ortega. El prelado convocó a toda la Iglesia que peregrina en esa arquidiócesis a celebrar el Jubileo del centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera. El documento señala que la solemnidad de Cristo Rey de este año coincide con la celebración de los beatos mártires mexicanos, el Día del Laico y la Jornada Mundial de la Juventud. Sin embargo, sostiene que la fecha adquiere una profundidad particular por cumplirse cien años del comienzo de la resistencia. La arquidiócesis de Guadalajara propone vivir el Jubileo como una experiencia de comunión eclesial, memoria agradecida y renovación de la fe. La convocatoria recuerda a quienes permanecieron fieles a Jesucristo y a la Iglesia hasta entregar su vida y reafirma el derecho del pueblo a celebrar, transmitir y vivir su fe tant

title: Carta Pastoral de los Obispos de México con motivo del centenario del inicio de la resistencia cristera – Infovaticana Blogs
summary: A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos mexicanos proponen leer aquel doloroso episodio histórico desde la verdad, la libertad de conciencia, la reconciliación y el compromiso d
summary_zh: 在基督徒抵抗运动开始一百年后，墨西哥主教们提议从真相、良心自由、和解与对话的角度来审视这段痛苦的历史事件。
title_zh: 墨西哥主教们在基督徒抵抗运动发起一百周年之际发表的牧函——Infovaticana博客
content: A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos mexicanos proponen leer aquel doloroso episodio histórico desde la verdad, la libertad de conciencia, la reconciliación y el compromiso de una fe dispuesta a hacerse servicio A cien años del inicio de la resistencia cristera, los obispos de México han dirigido al país una carta pastoral que busca recuperar uno de los episodios más dolorosos, complejos y controvertidos de la historia nacional sin convertirlo en instrumento de revancha, polarización o legitimación de la violencia. Bajo el título ¡Viva Cristo Rey! Su fe, nuestra memoria; su testimonio, nuestra misión, el documento propone una lectura histórica, teológica, espiritual, jurídica y pastoral de aquellos acontecimientos, pero, sobre todo, formula una pregunta dirigida a los creyentes de nuestro tiempo: ¿Qué significa hoy mantener viva una fe por la que otros estuvieron dispuestos a entregar la existencia? La carta no celebra la guerra ni presenta la resistencia armada como modelo de acción cristiana para el presente. Su punto de partida es otro, recordar la fidelidad de un pueblo que, en medio de la persecución, continuó rezando en sus hogares, bautizando a sus hijos, protegiendo a sus sacerdotes, celebrando clandestinamente los sacramentos y defendiendo la libertad de conciencia frente a un Estado que pretendió administrar las convicciones religiosas como si fueran una concesión del poder. Los obispos establecen desde el comienzo una diferencia indispensable entre el conflicto bélico, con sus errores, excesos, responsabilidades y heridas, y el testimonio de quienes murieron sin renunciar a su fe. Los mártires, subraya el documento, no son recordados porque hubieran matado por Cristo, sino porque murieron por Él y, en numerosos casos, perdonaron a sus verdugos. No se trata de recuperar un grito de guerra, sino la fuerza espiritual de una conciencia que se negó a ser sometida. El episcopado propone un triple ejercicio de memoria histórica, valoración del martirio y compromiso cristiano con la vida, la dignidad humana y la paz. Al recorrer la carta aparece una convicción transversal, la memoria solo es auténticamente cristiana cuando conduce a la conversión, ayuda a sanar las heridas, impide la repetición de las injusticias y se transforma en misión. Ese propósito exige comenzar por “un breve recuento del conflicto religioso”, título del primer capítulo y punto de entrada para entender que la confrontación no surgió repentinamente en 1926. Sus antecedentes se remontan a la formación del Estado mexicano después de la Independencia, cuando comenzaron a enfrentarse dos proyectos de nación. Uno reconocía al catolicismo como fundamento del orden social; el otro pretendía limitar la influencia institucional de la Iglesia para consolidar un Estado liberal, soberano y progresivamente secular. La Constitución de 1857 y las Leyes de Reforma representaron un momento decisivo en ese proceso. Establecieron la separación entre la Iglesia y el Estado, limitaron la propiedad eclesiástica y modificaron la presencia de la institución religiosa en la educación y la vida civil. Para sus promotores fueron disposiciones indispensables para modernizar al país; para la Iglesia y numerosos católicos significaron una intervención hostil sobre espacios que consideraban esenciales para su identidad y misión. La carta reconoce, sin embargo, que la secularización no ocurrió de manera inmediata ni eliminó el profundo arraigo del catolicismo en la vida nacional. La fe continuó presente en las costumbres, las familias, la educación, las fiestas y las formas comunitarias de organización. En ese contexto cobró fuerza el catolicismo social, inspirado en buena medida por la encíclica Rerum novarum de 1891. Surgieron organizaciones obreras, asociaciones juveniles y femeninas, cajas de ahorro para campesinos, escuelas nocturnas, centros de ayuda mutua, medios de comunicación y proyectos de participación política. title: San León Magno : el Papa que defendió la fe y la civilización cristiana – INFOVATICANA
summary: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —
summary_zh: 《致弗拉维安书》：基督论教义的基石利奥一世是一位具有非凡严谨性和深度的神学家。他写给君士坦丁堡牧首弗拉维安的著名教义书信——
title_zh: 圣良大帝：捍卫信仰和基督教文明的教宗 – INFOVATICANA
content: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —conocida como el Tomus ad Flavianum— definió con claridad la doctrina católica sobre las dos naturalezas de Cristo: divina y humana, unidas en una sola Persona. Este documento fue leído en el Concilio de Calcedonia (451) ante cientos de obispos que, al escucharlo, exclamaron: “Pedro ha hablado por boca de León.” Con esa expresión, la Iglesia universal reconocía el primado de la sede romana y la continuidad entre el Apóstol Pedro y sus sucesores. En tiempos en que el poder imperial pretendía someter la doctrina al control político, León reivindicó que la autoridad del Papa no depende del César ni de los concilios, sino de Cristo mismo, que prometió: “Tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta piedra edificaré mi Iglesia.” Gracias a su intervención, el Concilio de Calcedonia se convirtió en un hito de la ortodoxia cristológica y en un testimonio de la primacía del Romano Pontífice. El Papa León no impuso su autoridad con la fuerza, sino con la verdad; no por ambición humana, sino por fidelidad al depósito recibido. El Papa que detuvo a Atila En el año 452, la amenaza de los hunos llegó hasta las puertas de Italia. Atila, llamado “el azote de Dios”, había devastado Europa central y avanzaba hacia Roma. Sin ejército ni armas, León decidió ir al encuentro del invasor acompañado solo de algunos clérigos. El encuentro en el río Mincio, cerca de Mantua, se convirtió en uno de los episodios más sobrecogedores de la historia. La tradición narra que Atila, al ver al Papa, quedó sobrecogido por una fuerza sobrenatural y decidió retirarse. Algunos cronistas antiguos dicen que el caudillo vio detrás de León a los santos Pedro y Pablo empuñando espadas. Fuera cual fuera la causa, el hecho histórico es indiscutible: el Papa, solo con su autoridad moral, salvó a Roma de una destrucción segura. Tres años después, en el 455, León volvió a intervenir ante el vándalo Genserico, quien, aunque saqueó la ciudad, accedió a no incendiarla ni matar a sus habitantes. En una era de barbarie y desesperanza, el Papa se convirtió en defensor de la dignidad humana y de la civilización cristiana naciente. Un pastor de almas y doctor de la fe Más allá de los hechos históricos, el legado espiritual de León Magno se encuentra en sus Sermones y Cartas, textos que combinan rigor teológico, belleza retórica y profundidad pastoral. Sus homilías sobre la Encarnación y la Pascua son verdaderas joyas del pensamiento cristiano. En ellas resuena una teología que no separa la doctrina de la vida, ni la fe de la caridad. Fue también un reformador eclesial: disciplinó al clero, combatió los abusos, promovió la vida monástica y fortaleció la autoridad episcopal. Instituyó la solemnidad de la Natividad del Señor en Roma y consolidó la liturgia romana, que más tarde se extendería a toda la cristiandad. En un tiempo en que el caos amenazaba con disolver las instituciones, León mostró que la verdadera reforma de la Iglesia comienza en la santidad de sus pastores. De su espiritualidad brota una enseñanza perenne: el cristiano no puede dejarse arrastrar por el miedo ni por la confusión del mundo. Como escribió en una de sus homilías más célebres: “Reconoce, cristiano, tu dignidad. Y, puesto que has sido hecho partícipe de la naturaleza divina, no vuelvas a la antigua vileza con una conducta indigna.” En esas palabras se resume toda su visión: la fe no es una idea, sino una transformación de la persona; una participación real en la vida de Cristo. El Doctor que iluminó siglos León Magno murió el 10 de noviembre del año 461. Fue sepultado en la Basílica de San Pedro y proclamado Doctor de la Iglesia en el siglo XVIII por el Papa Benedicto XIV. Su influencia doctrinal se extendió por siglos y moldeó el pensamiento cristiano sobre el sacerdocio, la autoridad papal y la teología de la Encarnación. Su magi

title: El papa León XIV ya está en Argentina y el campo tuvo protagonismo en su primer discurso
summary: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país
summary_zh: 在访问乌拉圭之后，教宗利奥十四世于本周日开启了为期四天的历史性阿根廷之行，这是全球天主教会领袖首次踏上我国的土地。
title_zh: 教宗方济各已抵达阿根廷，他在首场讲话中重点谈及乡村问题。
content: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país desde Juan Pablo II en 1987. En ese marco, la primera actividad del Sumo Pontífice fue un discurso en el Palacio Libertad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA), frente al presidente de la Nación, Javier Milei. Y aunque sus palabras lógicamente estuvieron apuntadas hacia toda la sociedad, hubo numerosos pasajes que encontraron especial sintonía con el mundo agropecuario. Esto, en la previa de la reunión que León XIV mantendrá el lunes con representantes empresariales, sindicales y de organizaciones sociales, entre los que estarán los presidentes de las cuatro entidades de la Mesa de Enlace. EL PAPA LEÓN XIV EN ARGENTINA Puntualmente, el jefe mayor del Vaticano destacó el valor del esfuerzo cotidiano de los argentinos, con una mención expresa a quienes trabajan en el campo, y reivindicó la importancia de generar oportunidades, estimular la iniciativa privada y aprovechar responsablemente los recursos naturales. “Esta tierra conoce bien el valor del esfuerzo de quienes se ganan la vida en el campo y en las ciudades”, expresó León XIV, al destacar también el papel de los emprendedores y de las familias que sostienen sus hogares a través del trabajo. Asimismo, el Papa reconoció el enorme potencial productivo del país, al señalar que la Argentina cuenta con una extraordinaria riqueza natural, desde sus campos y reservas de agua hasta sus fuentes de energía, minerales y biodiversidad. Así, su mensaje combinó la posibilidad de aprovechar esos recursos para generar desarrollo y bienestar con la responsabilidad de preservar el ambiente y las condiciones de vida de las futuras generaciones. También dedicó un espacio a la innovación, la investigación y las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, destacando su capacidad para transformar la producción y mejorar la vida de las personas. Por otro lado, al expresar una mirada sobre América del Sur, mencionó además a los alimentos, la energía y el conocimiento como elementos que vinculan a los países y abren oportunidades para fortalecer la cooperación regional. LEON XIV, EL MARTÍN FIERO Y EL MATE Asimismo, León XIV ofreció referencias cargadas de simbolismo para la identidad argentina. Por ejemplo, mencionó al Martín Fierro de José Hernández, a Jorge Luis Borges, al tango y a las tradiciones del interior del país. Y no faltó una de las costumbres más arraigadas entre los argentinos: el mate compartido, al que presentó como un gesto cotidiano que favorece la conversación y la cercanía. Por último, hacia el final de su intervención, León XIV evocó a Nuestra Señora de Luján, patrona de la Argentina y figura de especial significado para las comunidades rurales y para generaciones de familias de todo el país. También recordó al papa Francisco, citó a Carlos Gardel y alentó a los argentinos a valorar el patrimonio recibido de las generaciones anteriores y trabajar para dejar un país mejor a quienes vendrán. content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. title: Santa Flora y Santa María de Córdoba : la fidelidad cristiana frente a la persecución islámica – INFOVATICANA
summary: La Córdoba del siglo IX: convivencia aparente, persecución real En la época del emirato independiente, la convivencia entre cristianos, judíos y musulmanes estaba condicionada por la legislación islám
summary_zh: 九世纪的科尔多瓦：表面上的共处，实际上的迫害在独立埃米尔国时期，基督徒、犹太人和穆斯林之间的共处受制于伊斯兰法律。
title_zh: 圣弗洛拉和圣玛丽亚·德·科尔多瓦：面对伊斯兰迫害的基督徒忠诚 – INFOVATICANA
content: La Córdoba del siglo IX: convivencia aparente, persecución real En la época del emirato independiente, la convivencia entre cristianos, judíos y musulmanes estaba condicionada por la legislación islámica. Los mozárabes podían mantener su culto, pero bajo estrictas limitaciones: pago de impuestos especiales, prohibición de construir nuevos templos, restricciones públicas y prohibición absoluta de cualquier palabra considerada ofensiva contra Mahoma o el islam. A partir de la década de 840, esta situación se endureció. Decenas de cristianos fueron arrestados por denunciar públicamente el islam o por profesar su fe sin ocultarla. Este movimiento espiritual, liderado por figuras como San Eulogio de Córdoba, defendía que ningún cristiano debía ocultar su fe por miedo al castigo. Dentro de este contexto se sitúan los martirios de Flora y María. Santa Flora: hija de padre musulmán y madre cristiana Flora nació en el seno de una familia mixta, lo que hacía especialmente peligrosa su confesión de fe. Según la ley islámica, era considerada musulmana por parte paterna, aunque hubiera sido educada en el cristianismo por su madre. Denunciar su fe ante las autoridades era, por tanto, considerado apostasía, delito castigado con la muerte. Tras denunciarla su propio hermano, Flora fue detenida y llevada ante el cadí. Se le ofreció el perdón a cambio de renunciar públicamente a Cristo. No solo rechazó la propuesta, sino que reafirmó con serenidad su fe cristiana. Fue encarcelada durante meses, sometida a presiones constantes y amenazas que no lograron quebrarla. Santa María: la monja perseguida que eligió el martirio María, también cristiana mozárabe, vivía consagrada a Dios en un monasterio femenino. Su hermana mayor, ya martirizada, había sido ejecutada por negarse a abandonar el cristianismo. María siguió su ejemplo. Fue detenida igualmente por “blasfemia contra el islam”, acusación habitual contra los cristianos que defendían sin miedo la fe. A diferencia de Flora, María sí pertenecía jurídicamente a la comunidad mozárabe, pero esto no la protegió: las autoridades consideraron sus palabras como una amenaza al orden político y religioso establecido. Unidas en el testimonio de Cristo Ambas jóvenes coincidieron en la cárcel, donde fortalecieron mutuamente su fe. San Eulogio —testigo excepcional de aquellos hechos— relató en sus Documentos Martiriales la entereza y serenidad con que Flora y María esperaron la sentencia. El 24 de noviembre del año 851 fueron decapitadas en Córdoba. Sus cuerpos fueron arrojados al río Guadalquivir para evitar que los cristianos los veneraran, pero las comunidades mozárabes mantuvieron viva su memoria. Con el tiempo, se incorporaron al grupo que la historia conoce como “los mártires de Córdoba”. ¿Por qué su testimonio sigue siendo actual? La historia de Flora y María no es un episodio marginal del pasado. Recuerda que la fe cristiana ha sido perseguida en la propia tierra española bajo sistemas políticos que se consideraban hegemónicos. Su martirio evidencia que la libertad religiosa no es un valor asegurado por defecto, sino una conquista que siempre puede verse amenazada. También interpelan a la Iglesia de hoy: ambas prefirieron la verdad a la supervivencia, la fidelidad a Cristo antes que la comodidad. Su ejemplo desmonta el mito de una “convivencia idílica” en Al-Ándalus, tan repetido en discursos culturales contemporáneos que omiten las limitaciones y represiones que sufrían los cristianos. Mártires mozárabes: raíz hispánica de una fe que resiste El martirio de Flora y María forma parte de una tradición martirial hispánica firme, cultivada durante las persecuciones romanas, prolongada bajo la ocupación islámica y viva todavía en los siglos modernos frente a otros totalitarismos. Su sangre es parte de la historia de España, de su identidad cristiana y de la fe que ha dado forma a su civilización. En un tiempo que relativiza todo, el testimonio de estas dos jóvenes devuelve claridad: Cristo merece ser confesad

title: RED WEEK PER RICORDARE I CRISTIANI PERSEGUITATI
summary: Anche quest’anno, nonostante il disinteresse dei media, dal 15 al 22 novembre la Fondazione Pontificia Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre ha dato vita al Red Week per ricordare che in tutto il mondo milioni
summary_zh: 今年，尽管媒体不感兴趣，但教宗基金会“援助受苦教会”仍于11月15日至22日举办了“红色周”活动，以提醒人们在全球范围内有数百万
title_zh: 红色周，纪念受迫害的基督徒
content: Anche quest’anno, nonostante il disinteresse dei media, dal 15 al 22 novembre la Fondazione Pontificia Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre ha dato vita al Red Week per ricordare che in tutto il mondo milioni di persone sono discriminate o perseguitate per la loro fede, in particolare le tante comunità cristiane che vivono in contesti dove la loro libertà religiosa subisce gravi violazioni. Per farlo, luoghi di culto, monumenti ed edifici pubblici in questa settimana si sono illuminate di rosso in tante nazioni contemporaneamente in occasione della Red Week, Dal 2015, sono stati illuminati luoghi di culto e monumenti fra i più iconici del mondo: dalla Fontana di Trevi a Roma al monumento del Cristo Redentore di Rio de Janeiro, dalla Basilica della Sagrada Familia di Barcellona a quella del Sacro Cuore di Parigi. La libertà religiosa in pericolo. Il Rapporto sulla libertà religiosa nel mondo 2025 di Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre evidenzia come in 62 Paesi si siano verificate violazioni sistematiche della libertà religiosa: 24 Paesi rientrano nella categoria più grave, ovvero quella di “persecuzione”, e 38 in quella di “discriminazione”. Complessivamente, oltre 5,4 miliardi di persone vivono in contesti in cui la libertà di religione è seriamente compromessa. 413 milioni di cristiani vivono in Paesi in cui la libertà religiosa è gravemente violata; di questi, circa 220 milioni risiedono in nazioni in cui sono direttamente esposti a persecuzioni. Regimi autoritari, violenza jihadista, nazionalismi religiosi e criminalità organizzata rappresentano oggi le principali minacce. Voci dimenticate: due serate tra musica e testimonianza a Milano e Roma Tra gli appuntamenti centrali della Red Week 2026 si sono svolte due serate di Voci dimenticate, il 16 novembre a Milano nella Basilica di Santa Maria delle Grazie, e il 21 novembre a Roma nella Basilica di San Saba. Chi lo desidera potrà contribuire, con una donazione libera, ai progetti di Aiuto alla Chiesa che Soffre a beneficio dei cristiani perseguitati. A Milano il pubblico ha assistito al concerto del Coro Filarmonico G.B. Pergolesi e dell’Orchestra Filarmonica Amadeus, diretti dal Maestro Gianmario Cavallaro; in programma brani del repertorio barocco, con musiche di Vivaldi, Torelli e Händel. Nella capitale il Coro Città di Roma, diretto dal Maestro Mauro Marchetti, ha proposto invece un percorso musicale con musiche di Mozart, Bach e Pergolesi. Ospite di entrambi gli appuntamenti è stata una donna che ha vissuto personalmente il dramma della persecuzione. La giovane sarà accompagnata da Don Joseph Fidelis Bature, sacerdote della diocesi nigeriana di Maiduguri e direttore del Trauma Center. La struttura, sostenuta dai benefattori di ACS, offre assistenza psicologica, spirituale e sociale alle vittime del gruppo terroristico islamista Boko Haram, accompagnandole in un percorso di guarigione e reinserimento nella comunità. Le loro toccanti testimonianze hanno raccontato la violenza che continua a colpire migliaia di persone e le occasioni di rinascita rese possibili dalla solidarietà di numerosi benefattori, italiani e internazionali. Le donazioni raccolte durante i due eventi di Milano e Roma sosterranno in particolare un progetto finanziato da ACS nella diocesi nigeriana di Minna, nel cui territorio le comunità cristiane vivono sotto la minaccia di attacchi armati, sequestri e violenze. L’iniziativa aiuterà 200 donne, uomini e bambini sopravvissuti alla violenza a ricostruire la propria vita attraverso il sostegno psicologico, il rafforzamento dei legami con la comunità e, per gli adulti, il recupero dell’autonomia economica. Il progetto prevede inoltre la formazione di circa 60 figure di riferimento delle comunità locali, tra cui sacerdoti e autorità, affinché sappiano riconoscere i bisogni delle persone più vulnerabili e offrire loro un sostegno adeguato. content: Un ami agnostique m’écrit pour me dire que j’ai décidément bien de la chance d’avoir la foi. Sa lettre arrive à un mauvais moment, car ces jours-ci ma foi est un combat. Je vais répondre à cet ami que je n’ai pas le temps de me demander si j’ai de la chance. Ce sont les athées qui ont de la chance. Ceux qui ne croient pas nous imaginent installés dans une sécurité imperturbable, propriétaires que nous serions d’une vérité qui nous dispenserait de penser. C’est tout le contraire. Un chrétien ne possède pas la vérité : c’est la Vérité qui le possède et cette Vérité ne le laisse pas souvent en paix.  La Vérité qui nous tient aux entrailles s’est incarnée dans un bébé ; elle a souffert sous Ponce Pilate, elle a été calomniée, elle a été crucifiée, elle est morte, elle est descendue aux enfers. content: La famille est un lieu de vie et de transmission, mais aussi un espace où chacun apprend à aimer et à grandir dans la foi. Conscient des défis auxquels les foyers sont aujourd’hui confrontés, le pape Léon XIV a rappelé,  lors de la messe célébrée à Buenos Aires le 9 novembre, combien les familles ont besoin de s’appuyer sur le Christ. Il a notamment lancé cet encouragement : « Ne vous résignez pas face aux voix qui ne cessent de répéter que la famille chrétienne est dépassée. Au contraire, aujourd’hui plus que jamais, elle représente un pilier au milieu des nombreuses précarités de notre époque. » Le Saint-Père a également rappelé que les familles sont « un lieu privilégié pour connaître et rencontrer le Christ », et les a encouragées à transmettre la foi « au même titre que la vie ». summary: By Charles Gardner — A former pop star and model has spoken of her love for Jesus despite being brought up to attend synagogue.
